原文: His dismay is painted in broad strokes on his aging face.
Godwif sneers.
Sounds like you've grasped the general idea. What shall we do with you, Leofric?
You made a mistake, but it's all right. We're here now. I forgive you.
A murmur rises among the crowd.
For all my flippancy, I must admit this is pretty much what I expected. Last summer we would have put up a much better fight, but the winter has taken its toll on us.
I'm trying to redeem the boy, you daft bastard. If we just kill him his soul will be lost!

You rest the back of your hand on her forehead, feeling her fever against your skin - it's not the worst fever you've ever felt, but if it's lasted for several weeks, it's no small wonder she's so tired.
You are our thegn. We follow you as long as we live.
I hope he didn't suffer.
I'll be back if I need anything.
What, are you too important to announce yourself when you break into an old man's home?
Wait, [i]she[/i] set the fire?
The man is holding the broomstick in front of himself like he's trying to hide behind it.
I'm afraid we'll have to. Hopefully the spirits will forgive us.
Nefja isn't receptive to that sort of thing.
Thank you, your highness. We're always happy to serve the Jarl.
Heads lowered, the three thralls appear to accept their new fate. They pick up only what they can carry and set off up towards your camp.
Howling Witch
These men are all a bit worse for wear, but they seem to have a lot of armed combat experience.
Your crew rows as fast as they can, but the other ship outpaces [Shipname] by a large margin.
He releases his grip, eyes searching your face.
She gives you a crooked smile.
What did you expect? No matter what we do for these people, we'll never be more than filthy heathens to them.
Well... I suppose that's that then. I thank you for looking into it all the same.
{Pull him out.}
King Osred's terms are simple. Die!
Damn right it does! Let's kick these Northumbrian weak-pissers out of here!
The gate will not withstand a direct attack, but breaking it down will surely alert the village. Do you wish to destroy the gate?
The shieldmaiden Vigundr was killed in Frisia, wielding this winged spear against unknown attackers. Her husband sold it to you in Ribe so he could afford the journey home.
No. Of course I can't. Of course you're right, I only... we've searched for a place for so long.
That whole thing with me being her "elfin knight"? What title did she grant you, her Faerie Princess? She's obsessed with these whimsical tales.
Sounds good - lead the way.
When the fighting is over and the last of Osred's forces scatter, she is nowhere to be seen among the dead.
I'm just glad you're both alive and well. One feud is about as much as this clan can handle, I think.
What is the purpose of having a fortress if anyone can enter?!
Astridr holds up a hand and makes a pause to steel herself.
Why?
"See, where they sit beneath the hall-gable, protecting themselves with the pillar in front?" The pillar split at the giant's gaze, and the pillar-beam broke in two.
You had your chance to get out of this alive. Now you wont.
Eydis' Clothes
We will sweep through the village like a plague, leaving none alive.
All right, we'll take the deal. We figure: if this is some trick, we're good at running. We'll find our way back here just fine.
Oh yes! I'm glad you were listening!
I don't wish to impose upon a [Player:man/woman] of your standing, but you fascinate me. Will you consider lending me your aid?
Go on then, have your fun. I'll go and rendezvous with Skallagrimr.
That behaviour does you no credit. No credit to your clan, either!
You'd better not.
It will be a trifling matter for one such as you.
Nefja takes a deep breath.
Let's see what happens. It's good to know you've got my back.
The young witch shrugs and turns her attention back to her food.
Indeed. Well, that's... hm.
I have a special place in my heart for converts. Yours was a soul that once hung in a kind of limbo, but now you are saved.
We ought to go back at once! It's impossible to say what might befall us on the way.
He's a pale fellow. No wonder, when him and his didn't want to eat or drink.
[i]No.[/i] No I will not. Christians or nae, you're strangers to me.
You can put that [Player:weapon] away, love. An old woman is no threat to your kind.
Keep that up, you might actually hurt someone!
We're looking for your druid. We seek an audience with him.
So the other day, down at the docks--
You both drink again, and the poison induces another coughing fit in Ingimarr. After he recovers, he sways slightly, eyes his cup suspiciously, and then finally understands what you've done.

The assholes in the tunnels had us build a giant scaffold, but never paid us. We're not exactly equipped to take them on, so to speak, and we don't really have the means to leave, as we were relying on their payment to get us out of here.
You'd better not try to stop me...
This is all the proof we need that Saint Remus is the one we should [i]really[/i] worship!
Just be careful. It's dangerous over there.
I have my doubts that we would even still be alive without Eydis here. I mean I'm not even talking about the cooking, but just her general aura of calm and common sense.
She certainly gave me that impression.
I'll deal with it. Maybe lay off the ale.
You little shit! Did you see that kid?! She just nicked your stuff!
Nefja grunts from the side.
Without warriors to support us, our alliance will seem hollow - toothless.
Found anything?
I'll not invite such a ship into my harbour! I thank you for asking permission, but none will be granted, and if you try to land here anyway, your ship will be attacked and sunk.
He exhales sharply.
I knew as soon as I first saw you that you were someone special.
She's troubled us long enough from the sidelines. It's time we end her meddling.
The last sentry falls, and the silence is broken only by the rush of wind through the crags.
He grasps you firmly by the wrist.
{Give 50 Rations.} I wish to give an offering to Heimdallr that he may grant me vigilance.
No. I'm sure you haven't.
You've done a noble thing here today. Some of the Legionnaires saw it all and told us of your actions.
Find at least three different trees in Skjern Forest.
You can see his jaw tighten.
Breach
Can I trust you Gunnarr?
His mock suspicion melts into a warm smile.
The invasion is called off. I've chosen to maintain our alliance with the Picts.
The old hag screams so spittle flies from her mouth.
Aye, ekki at dakka. Just be careful out there.
That's [Player:Father]'s, isn't it? But your uncle brought his body home. This can't be him.
It looks like things are really coming together. Torfinn has already laid down the hull of the new ship - [Shipname], was it?
Few of them would benefit from making this a smooth transition. It will be important to know where they stand.
Well, I hope you've made peace with the gods, because I've been looking forward to this for a long time.
Hrodgærda casually turns her back on you both and casts a long look towards the church.

The moment you unsheathe your seax, Geirmundr jumps back, hands raised. He hesitates for the blink of an eye, then he turns and hurls himself head-first into the bonfire, screaming for Surtr to take him.
A gleam of gold shimmers in Maban's eyes.
Aye, I'm she. Why do you ask?
Let me take a look.
Enough! Enough. I yield.
What are you thinking? Pick them off from a distance?
Evasion Failed
All tension in the hall is immediately transformed to relief and happiness. Grainne slaps you affectionately on the arm.

The air is so thick with hostility you might carve it with a knife. In the tense silence, a distant rumble reverberates through a cave exit behind Grainne - your allies marching through the ravine below.
You're awake!
I'm sorry... I needed the courage, but I shouldn't have made you drink as well. Next time will be different.
I'll see when I get around to it.
I suppose that won't hurt - just don't expect any discounts on account of your reputation. Show me what you need.
Let's see how close we can get to the tent without being seen.
Now, take your ship to the bay where the river Tay runs towards the seat of the Pictish king, and follow the coast towards the north for a long way.
Only take care not to disturb the King's grave unless you know in your heart that you are worthy of his legacy.
Indeed, you shouldn't. If I need something, I'll come to you.
Pitchforks were never really meant to be used in combat, but sometimes you have to use what's at hand.
Get out of my sight, raider. Leave Orkneyjar and never come back!
I heard [Player:Name] spared a man [Player:he/she] defeated. Even let him join [Player:his/her] hird.
We're here to help you take Dun Phris.
How are you doing today?
Whatever I can get my hands on. I've been setting up a steady supply of food from the outlying farms.
Your hird is gathered around your mother. Astridr looks distraught.
It's good to see you again, my friend. I hope you haven't changed your mind. As I said, we have nowhere to go.
How does [i]that[/i] settle it? That must have been a nightmare! For all you know she may have got up to piss and a bird happened to take off outside and wake the girl up.
In a manner of speaking - I build such items to order. You can bring me the materials I need, and I will make whatever equipment you require.
All the more reason to strike now, while they are weak. Let Osred and Æthelred bicker over whose head the crown fits better. Soon, it won't matter.
Leofric, the champion of Eoforwic, has challenged your hird to a practice fight, to see what you're made of.
My name is Maucolyn, I am the gerefa of this town.
You're free to leave. I don't care where you go, but you better get out of my town.
Too risky. We'll approach in the open and see if they listen to reason.
The war has begun, [Player:Name]! No need to tell me what transpired in Dun Phris, my messengers have already told me everything.
His voice is dry and raspy.
I'll pretend I didn't notice that insult. Show me your wares so we can get this over with.
Once you've both cleaned up and had breakfast, Kyre fetches a gift from the back of her house.
Lord of Seals
I can't promise anything.
The pool of water is shallow at first, but quickly deepens. Underneath the water, a tunnel extends further into the cave. The water has a slightly unpleasant colour and smells stagnant.
Royal advisor is a respected position. You'll be duly rewarded.
{Attack.}
I don't see a way around a fight.
The other man appears to regain his wits.
Torfinn would be the most important voice to hear in this matter, I'd say. I'm sure he has some ideas.
And in return?
You and your people - you left us alone to face the vengeance of Conall's warriors! Who were they to know you put my dear Leannan up to that!
Are you fully aware of what you've gotten yourself into? Kyre is beautiful, that's true, but she's not... normal.
Gunnarr steps forward.
That took an unexpected turn.
{Attempt to kill Erlingr with a surprise attack, starting a fight.}
But your father was lax in his rule, and I admired that. He may not have built a strong and fearsome clan, but he respected us and put great trust in us all.
Well we're glad to have you on board.
We'll help you fight them if that's what you want, but those who survive will not be executed. Agreed?
I have not been entrusted with that information, but I have been assured that you will like it.
The surviving raiders have turned up in Ribe. This is your chance at revenge, if you want it.
I'm going to bed, Ketill. Let's talk tomorrow.
Grimulfr sheathes his weapon and leans back against a tree, suddenly looking much older than he is.
There's a beacon on the cliff that's meant to be lit in the fog, so ships can avoid the rocks.
I didn't want this. I wish you'd stayed with us.
Asleifr simply nods once, then he returns his attention to his companions.
Sorry, my young man! Let me just rest my arthritic 25-year-old legs a moment before I leave.
Bring Hulda some flowers from near the animal pen.
Skule did you a great disservice in sending you here. He should have come himself.
[i][Player:Name]![/i]
We're close now. If our strategy works, and your murder of Caustantin is successful, this may be a short war indeed.
You won't be converting us.
It was.
We'll get you out of there. Have faith in it.
It's mostly silver jewellery and my old sword. You can keep all that, just bring me that claw, I beg you.
My name is Kyre, widow of the merchant Baldred - I am honoured to meet you.
I just saw those boys come through camp and leave out the north-west entrance in a damn hurry.
He'd better accept his punishment, or his entire family will pay for it.
As I thought - your "guests" carry a legion's worth of steel into my home. Have you no thought for the safety of an old man, Cillian? Fool boy!
You can't feel a battle in your bones or foresee a fight.
Ah, indeed. Then I'm sorry to be the one to tell you, but that grave is closed under my protection, and that of our community.
A search of the nearby area turns up a broken cart that has been stripped of valuables.
Eanbald makes the sign of the cross and mumbles a few words in Latin.
If you stick around, I'll be able to find you again in case I need you.
Skule Skullcleaver is behind this. He's been working against us for months.
Grainne looks like she's had it with your bullshit. She raises a closed fist and a loud whistle escapes her lips. The result manifests immediately.
Skule is a very impressive man in the flesh.
Always happy to serve a friend. What else can I do for you?
Rurik shakes his head and drops his knife on the floor in disgust.
The young man seems to relax and makes a motion with his hand for the others to sit back down, which they reluctantly do.
Do you wish to set sail and leave Jutland?
You think that was a good hit? Wait 'till I'm warmed up!
Where [Victim:Name] was walking moments before, all you now see is a long jagged hole in the ice. The rest of your hird quickly covers the rest of the distance to the shore.
{Pay 100 Valuables.} Here you go.
So you know about them? Why in the Allfather's name have you not addressed this yet?
Sounds good. That'll get us very close to the king's hall.
Relief and gratitude mingle awkwardly on his face.
{Kill him.}
Well, what are you looking for?
Let's go and see if Skallagrimr's hird is back.
If we are to attack Jelling, we must do it quickly and unexpectedly.
I may help you after all. Who did you say you were looking for?
They said the tomb was protected by dwarves or elves or other such underground creatures - that horrible vengeance would befall any who dared to breach its sanctity.
Verca, love - go get Wiala and your parents.
Everyone load up. We're cleaning the place out.
One of them, a young man of about 18 winters, looks up from the fire and stands to address you. The others remain seated, but exchange sideways looks.
Challenge Nukki.
A mysterious tincture that fills the user with vigour, allowing them to move faster for 3 turns.
He did.
Hides've gone missing again. There's a thief in town.
This is not good.
It's an honour to finally meet you. My father speaks of you in glowing terms.
Finnguala is with her future husband. They seem to have known each other for a long time.
No need to thank me. We just did as Caustantin asked.
Ljotr and I will keep an eye on them, I'll let you know if anything changes.
For that alone, you will not leave this place alive.
She grimaces.
Aye, just what I had in mind.
No. They know we're coming, but they won't be expecting [i]us[/i].
The trader throws his hands up in triumph.
On the other hand, a meadhall would be a great way to build up prestige at home and strengthen relations with our neighbours. Everybody loves a good feast!
Seeking Sanctuary
He claps his hands together, startling a couple of crows off a nearby tree.
You don't understand! We have nothing left to give them!
You shouldn't have run, Aife. You'll pay with your life for turning your back on me.
Engraved Rusty Sword
[Greedy:Name] leans in close.
And we'll be bringing so much treasure, the ship will barely remain afloat on the return trip!
You have an outstanding debt to Cuthrad and I'm here to collect.
Enough! Archers, loose!
The wide blade of this chisel makes for very poor stabbing. All the more embarrassing to be killed with it.
Then you'll need a byname instead.
Let's bring her, [Player:Name]. Eydis' cooking will make the journey easier if nothing else.
Sorry my [Player:boy/girl], you were almost there, but you skipped the second to last part! No true Christian would make such a mistake.
[Player:Velkominn/Velkomin] to Ribe, [Player:Name]. To what do we owe the pleasure of your visit?
Your hird gradually wakes up and assembles for breakfast around the campfire. That's when it hits you.
A look of grim realisation comes over him.
Røskva closes her hand around the jar.
We should go back and check on her.
Four hours later, Skallagrimr emerges from your main force camped below.
It's kind of you to say that, but I grieve for Hulda. She is a wise woman, with a lifetime of knowledge of the plants, the gods, and the spirits. I hate to see her mind unravel like this.
But you look strong. Ever try your hand at farm work?
Deer is scarcer than usual on account of the wolves, but on the other hand I can't loose an arrow without hitting a grouse this season, so I'm not complaining.
Of course he will, otherwise what would be the point?
Gunnarr raises his [Leader:weapon] in salute.
A toast, to the unwitting generosity of the jarl!

Ribe's town crier is an energetic young woman with fiery red hair. Her sharp features are dotted with freckles and her smile spells mischief. Her trained voice carries easily across the din of the market.
When word of this raid spreads, we'll have no trouble mustering a great army. You'll soon be in command of the greatest army the north has seen since Bravellir!
He's dead. Murdered by men working for a rival thegn.
People went missing in the marsh?
There is a sharp edge to [ObjectOfAffection:Name]'s voice.
The old smith glares from the back of the smithy.

Myrddin was here before us. Far as I know he's always lived in that little cave. And the problem is, everyone here is all Christian of course - fervently so. They don't understand Myrddin, but he frightens them.
[Stuck:He/She] braces for the fall, but [Stuck:his/her] arm lands at a bad angle. There is a sickening crunch. [Stuck:Name] grunts loudly and clutches [Stuck:his/her] arm.
[Leader:Name] walks up to the cell and looks the young boy right in the eyes.
The doubts. The bickering.
Don't leave me standing here too long.
Behind you, your mother is staring wide-eyed into the distance, frozen in fear for her son's fate.
Not yet.
Tell me about your home.

Thanks to you, Northumbria and Pictavia is unified under one king. Soon, a great victory feast will take place, and you are a guest of honour. This could be the perfect opportunity to invade and seize power for yourself.
Been in town for a while, come in from Aars and Viborg.

Two boys, one around 15 years of age, the other much younger, are crouched at the edge of the creek. A moment's observation reveals their errand: the older boy is teaching the younger how to tickle fish. The lesson is confined to a purely theoretical level, as the creek is much too shallow for fish.
Thank you for your help. I... I have nothing more to offer you than that.
I thought you might be my contact, when I saw you enter Æthelred's camp. Let's get this over with.
He is round of belly and red of cheeks, with a friendly smile permanently affixed to his face, and a voice that booms across the busiest part of Market Street without at any point becoming obnoxious.
Kveldulfr's Cured Armour
{Give 4000 Valuables.} Fair enough.
Oooh look at yeeww, all dressed up fer a meetin' with the other fancy-pants.
Who should help you repair the mast?
When you and my daughter reach Perth, find my niece Mael Fabaill. She sells the products of our lands by the river, and she'll reward you for your great deeds.
If we stand our ground here, it will lead only to chaos. We will find a new place, better suited to our goals, and--
Everyone looks up as you leave the tent together and head out to the water to wash.
There is no mistaking the tree the gydja mentioned - it looks like it has stood in this place forever, its gnarly roots protruding from the mushy soil far around it.
A man and a woman stand very close in front of a stack of barrels with ale. It takes no more than a split second's glance to see that these two people [i]really[/i] want to fuck each other.
She will fetch fresh, healthy horses from one of the nearby farms. They will be waiting for you at the edge of town when you leave.
End the Feast
Grainne nods stoically and dies without uttering another word. In her last moments, she seems almost relieved to meet the fate she must have expected for many years.
The merchant Jardarr Jarnskeggason is looking for strong warriors to reclaim his property.
The... convent.
No, no, no! W-wait! We can pay you!
It takes a while, but you pull down the nid-pole and carve up the slaughtered horse for meat. The cawing of crows follows you as you leave the remains to the scavengers.
Grimkell and Olbjorn seem to contemplate this for a moment. Asleifr nods sagely.
The fisherman is minding his own business cleaning a well worn net. He looks up and nods politely - though with a somewhat worried expression on his face.
The people of Dun Phris eagerly await your decision.
We need such a cure as much as you do. I will not give it up.
Don't get ahead of yourself, we're not done yet.
Just as well. I never understood why we brought him with us in the first place.
That is regrettable, but I understand. Doubtlessly, you fear giving away your tactics to one who may be your enemy in the future.
Asleifr clears his throat.
Røskva's voice is a low sing-song, barely loud enough for you to hear.
Ketill's eyes search the old man's face.
Did you hear about what happened to Beorhtfrith's son? They say he got too close to the river. Never seen again.
Her eyes wander aimlessly.
Stay calm, the bishop sent us.
{Buy helmet for 60 Valuables.} What do you say to 6 ørtug of silver for that helmet?
That's... god damn [i]terrible[/i] news!
In the back, the youngest of Erlingr's sons, Are, is looking increasingly distraught.
Who are you?
Speak to Æthelred in Eoforwic.
Looters have come to the ruins of Donncoirce's homestead to scavenge the ashes for surviving valuables. The Princess's guardsman Bressal has begged you to chase them out of his King's home.
I uhm... I'm sure I don't understand your question. But I will eh... keep in mind that you asked.
That's your problem, I've done what I can.
Let me take a look at your stock of materials.
{Kill him.} I sentence you to death.
It takes you a moment to locate where Leofric fell. Surprisingly, the Champion of Eoforwic still breathes.
We can drink together once you swear fealty to me.
Talk to Astridr to end the campaign.
You must be [Player:Name]! Godwif asked us to find you and help you breach the walls!
Why did my father bring you with him?
Are you suggesting we rout these bandits?
My family has worked the forest outside Ribe for many years. We helped build this town.
If I don't make it, take care of my boys.
In Northumbria, you've discovered evidence of your father's final expedition. Perhaps you can find out where it all ended and get some answers at last.
He clenches his fists. His expression could reflect anger, but you think it may in fact be shame.
I was here for-- treasure. But the robbers took it. If you help me, I'll... [i]gasp[/i]... I'll tell you how to find it.
{Leave.} Very well.

My father is no longer a young man, of course. I know his opinion is that I should stay here and help with the farm. But now he sees the results of our travels, his complaints have grown less vehement.
Don't try anything, pagan.
Who does it belong to? It's so cool!
You have reached Deva Victrix - a grand fortress of the old empire, sadly abandoned many centuries ago. The Legion of Romulus has reclaimed the ruins as a holy site to honour Saint Romulus.
Sigridr the huntress has found a group of travellers camping in the forest near your homestead.
He glances at his guards, then back to you.
Anything else?
Return to Skjern and speak to Astridr to end your adventures in Britain.
Good. And just so there's no mistake: if you change your mind, we will burn Dun Phris to the ground, kill everyone who resists, and take the rest as thralls.
Confront the hunters.
She's... got a lot to prove, right? Seems like it anyway. She's tough as nails but she doesn't seem to know it.
Speak.
You didn't hear? Someone left an ox's head there last night.
Good. Cats are skilled hunters, she'll be just fine on her own.
Caustantin strokes his beard pensively.

The group enters Eoforwic's dungeon through a tunnel near the river - back in the Roman times, this used to be a sewer, and the stench of offal and human waste still lingers like the memory of a nightmare.
Of course.
Didn't Grainne say he had an army?
As you wish.
It was a mistake to think your kind could bring anything but death and treachery to these lands. We should have killed you all the moment you set foot on our shores!
Go on.
[Superstitious:Name] is working nearby, keeping a close and increasingly suspicious eye on Morcant - a fact that clearly hasn't escaped the captive monk.
Caustantin has an underground treasury. It's [i]our[/i] right to plunder it.
Look, I don't know you well enough to offer much. Can't send strangers out to enforce the King's justice.
I did business with your father. More than a few of your houses are built with my lumber.
You brought him in alive! Well done. Here's your 98 pence, as promised.
That [i]bikkju-sonr[/i]!
Osred is still alive, but only barely. He lies unconscious in a pool of his own blood.
And what of my companions? Are they guilty by association?
You're not the first man who's come here and tried to wrest control of Orkneyjar away from me. In fact I myself took it from a man called Vidarr, who took it from the Picts.
I'm reminded of the first time we met, on the road to Perth, [Player:Name]. I now realise that could've turned out a lot worse for me.
Something is amiss. Why were the beacons not lit in warning? And the timing is so very [i]convenient[/i] for our enemies.
Realising what she just said, Røskva blushes slightly and hides a smile with her hand.
Let's hope so.
She blinks, trying to gather her thoughts.
Indeed, well, it would be best if you were to explore some other kingdom. My realm is thoroughly charted already, and my subjects will not appreciate your band of warriors roaming the countryside.
Name your price.
No fish will bite my hooks... haven't done so for months.
That's about the size of it.
Who were you meeting?
Cillian stops to think on it, and the local firefly population breathes a sigh of relief. His jar already buzzes with half a dozen of them.
"Welcome, Hymir, in fine fettle: now your son has come home to your halls, one we've both missed on his long travels. Hród's adversary has come along with him, a fighter's friend, Thorr is his name."
Who cares? They pose no threat to us anymore.
{Attack.} Sorry Dubglas, we're saving your cousin.
{Show Sefa's necklace.} I have a question first. Have you ever seen a necklace like this?
He gives a wheezing laugh that is tinged with bitterness.
You've managed to outdo my worst expectations. Well... this is as far as you'll get!
As Ingimarr glances away, you deftly exchange his drinking horn for yours and raise it in a salute, the old man none the wiser to your ruse.
[Boring:Name] manages to grab [Greedy:Name]'s shoulder.
Yes, your majesty. I swear to God.
Steal the jewelled gold cross from the warehouse outside the southern wall.
Thank you, [Player:Norseman/Norsewoman]. Now leave us in peace to pray for our souls.
We still need to find that glade, of course - if any of it still remains. I doubt any Christians were here when this stone was erected.
They've sworn it.
Really?! Hahah! That's excellent news! I can't wait to get off this rainy, windy shitshow of an island.
All right, I'll help you ferret out that spy.
If he's making for Hedeby, he'd have to cross through the marsh...
You haven't seen the last of us!
Ketill raises an eyebrow.
{Examine the tracks.}
As the last of your enemies falls and the sound of rushing blood in your ears subsides, you suddenly become aware that another fight is taking place nearby.
If you want me to undertake this project, I will meet you in the forest and help you choose a suitable tree. If I start immediately, I should be able to have your ship ready by the late spring.
Giants!
Be reasonable. We're honourable people, we've come to establish ties between our nations. Let us help you.
Ketill gratefully wraps his arms around you. His hands grasp your shirt and you can feel his breathing grow steadier. He mumbles into your shoulder.
I'm glad to finally be rid of the old fool.
You are much too young a man to be so cynical.
You're a good [Player:man/woman]. You did your best.
My own lands have just as much intrigue and plotting as yours - if not more.
Shortly after night fall...
The young man nods resolutely and saunters away in the direction of the temple.
No! I was as surprised as you when the king ordered your arrest.
So, your home - Skjern, wasn't it? You're the thegn there? How did that come to pass?
'Sides... numbers will do little at this point. The way they've dug in, only cunning can save you.
Fine. I'll find out what happened to him, one way or another.
Asleifr releases you from his embrace and crosses his arms.
Well at least [Player:he/she]'s [i]sorry[/i] for leaving us to die.
Welcome back. After what happened in Dun Phris, I thought it would be pertinent to start planning for the invasion.
That's a good idea, but I know little about hunting with traps. Is that something you can handle?
Lost in his own thoughts, it takes him a while to focus his eyes on you.
But if the king should raise the leidangr army tomorrow, how many ablebodied warriors could our clan muster? A dozen?
No! Don't! Nobody has to die here! We can-- don't make me fight these people!!
Find Æthelred and see what Osred's fate will be.
Not that it stopped him from taking my maidenhood.
The girl returns to the other thralls, still sobbing, but relieved. Everything quickly settles down.
Return to the priest and tell him you've decided to let the cult stay.
You helped us when you did not have to - in spite of the gold and influence the Halfdansons hold. There is justice in these lands yet. Thank you!
Fortunately your sacks are empty of looted treasure, all trinkets having been secreted about your persons. The guards are visibly relieved.
All right, well, half of it belongs to me, as per our arrangement.
How many are they?
You've told me almost nothing of your lands.
With a sigh and a longing glance at [ObjectOfAffection:Name], Kyre disappears back into her home.
Cailtram mac Muircholaig? Oh aye, I may know his girl.
You'll be gydja of Skjern one day. Attend so many you'll get sick of 'em.
Tried to defend himself, then run away. Got tripped up and savaged.
Just do me a favour and don't settle down with a gaggle of kids any time soon, all right? I don't want to lose both of my best friends all at once.
We better stay clear then. Thanks for the warning!
Visit Bjørgdis and inquire about her daughter's health.
{Kill him.} How about I just take everything!
Ketill stares wide-eyed at the loot.
I'm not in the business of helping people.
Her face turns quite a strong shade of red.
Stand down, you fools! We seek only the treatment for a disease that plagues my family!
I'm ready to get out of here, you ready to get out of here? Because I'm ready to get out of here!
I know that's just crazy dream-logic, but a part of me can totally believe that's what would happen.

I will not squander the trust you've placed in me. Your lives and your health are my main concern. We're all hoping for wealth and glory, but what use are such things if we are not alive and well to enjoy them?
We will [i]never[/i] permit heathen warriors to enter Perth! You will be vanquished! Our king depends upon us!
Perhaps we [i]should[/i] unite our territories. But [i]I[/i] will be in charge.

With a great cheer, everyone dips into the drink. A few extra pieces of meat are also thrown into a pot and cooked over the roaring fire.
Ugh that is the worst. I'm really gonna regret finishing this.
The are signs of struggle and panic throughout the grubby alleyway, but your attention is drawn to bloody tracks leading along the wall, down toward the river.
Young fools. Do you not see what you've done?
Thanks again for stepping in. Pig's not worth spilling blood, no matter how our families get on.
All right. I'm done. Let's get out of here.
I'll travel back to the others and let them know what's happened.  We'll get you out of there, I promise.
I observed your audience with the king. You'll make no headway with him. Æthelred is much more reasonable.
I understand. Something greater than love or desire pulls you away from me. I'm well used to the tragedies of life.
Do you have so little faith in your patron? The monuments of his empire rise from the soil everywhere in these lands. Finding a new home should not be so difficult.
The favour of the gods is not granted freely. You may return any time, when you can present a worthy offering.
He holds up a hand in salute without turning around.
{Examine the body.}
Does this mean we can meet Valerius now?
Danr's deadpan is impeccable.
I've been looking for you.
Eydis looks like she very much wants you all to know she doesn't give a rat's ass what you youngsters get up to in the night.
Leofric may be dead, but more guards doubtlessly await us inside.
You stand victorious side by side with your father and his long-dead hird. Slain jøtnar smolder on the ground, their faces distorted into expressions of pain and surprise.
Always happy to help an ally.
Do you happen to know a girl who's friends with a man called Cailtram?
Here, this is all she stole. Take it and leave.
[i]Sancta Maria Mater Dei ora pro nobis peccatoribus nunc et in hora mortis nostrae.[/i]
He's somewhere in his late 20's, dressed in well-worn armour, and with a ghastly scar along the jaw where a spear once sliced it open.
The leader of the fyrd is an old man with a tight, muscular build and hands that look accustomed to hard labour. He's missing his right eye.
Are you Theodore?
Thank you, [Player:Norseman/Norsewoman]. Perhaps there is hope for your soul after all.
I don't really have anything in mind.
Both! They stole our cargo, and that forced us to steal from them - to survive! We're stuck here, no ship, no horses, no cargo to buy our way home. Tell me: what choice do we have?
{Evaluate your surroundings.}
I don't send others to do my fighting, if that's what you're getting at.
The young witch frowns.
The noise of the crumbling wall fills the tunnels and the guards jump to their feet, frightened.
Thegn Skule encroaches upon my territory - I am forced to seek aid elsewhere.

An emissary of Osred is meeting a group of Mercians to gain their support against Æthelred's impending coup. This cannot be allowed to happen, so you are tasked to interrupt the negotiations and kill everyone in attendence.
His voice is slurred and his tone unsteady.
By the Æsir, the rumours were true.
The Godi looks at you, his demeanor anxious.
He's not getting up from that one. Thegn Skule is dead.
The thralls watch you warily, unsure of what fate you have in store for them. A young man, with only the sorry beginnings of a beard on his chin steps forward tentatively.
Avenge the murder of your uncle Grimulfr.
I'll make the decision when we're all aboard.
Toll for passing our land... their goods and their lives!
Røskva - see what you can do to help.
She was walking through a meadow naked. There were ravens circling her.
Discuss Ragnvaldr's information with your huscarls.
I should get on with it.
Interrogate a captured Norwegian raider.
Ketill West-man.
I have no interest in speaking with your king.
Grave Flower
If you seek more information, you can talk to the priest in charge or the leader of the fyrd. They're talking in the back.
Røskva releases a shuddering breath of frustration, spins angrily on the spot, and disappears off into the forest on her own.
What do you sell?
I'll return if I need something.
Yes. That is what I have heard as well. Pray tell, if I were to call the leidangr army tomorrow, how many trained and equipped warriors could your territories contribute?
It's good you got it over with.
Naked bone, chipped and weathered is all that is left. Pieces have been scattered by the attention of hungry scavengers, and the darkened soil has drunk most of the fluids otherwise spilled.
{Go to your tent with Ketill.}
Jumper eyes you suspiciously as you inch closer to him, and he shifts his weight in anticipation of your treachery.
Will you give me your account of it, then?
Sounds like a worthy challenge.
Unsavoury Dealings
Ingimarr is pretending to be pre-occupied with his mead, but you can tell he's straining to listen in.
Fine, I'll just shut up forever then!
So you can use it against me? How about we sort this all out after the fight, eh? Unless I die - then you can just take it from my cold, dead hands!
{Cancel.}
Ancient Helmet
Strangers... please help...
Meet the godi's son at the watch tower north of the hamlet.
Let me see what you have.
The [Unlucky:archetype] manages to grab hold of the rope without any problems, and with your help, you manage to get [Unlucky:him/her] to safety moments later.
The enemy suffered at least a half dozen times as many losses. Our tactics certainly paid off!
Barghest?
He puts down his woodwork with a loud smack and turns to face you. Anger flares briefly in his eyes before he calms himself.
Hrodgærda. Skule's killer.
One free man or woman, or the lives of three thralls. That is the price to enter the tomb. Pay it, or leave.
She smiles - and it's a proper smile for once, showing teeth and everything.
Clearly out of breath, she greets you with a small nod.
Skule maintains a polite blank facial expression.
Is there anything you need done around the place?
Need a drink?

Even though the man just about sees your right hook coming, the strength of your swing offers him no chance to defend against it. A loud smack emanates as your fist connects with his jaw, and he's out cold at once.
We should take what we came for and get out of here.
Increases Strength for 3 turns. Use twice for double effect, but this reduces Finesse and Sense for the rest of the fight.
You're enjoying a rare moment of respite in the company of a bowl of nice hot stew when Nefja lowers herself down next to you with a weary groan.
We're done. Get out of here.
A sturdy broad-masked net suspended by a rope. The victim is ensnared until the end of the next turn.
Could've gone worse.
If you need to enter Jelling in secret, look for a small farmhouse on the left off the path to the southern gate.
Thank you, dad. I miss you.
Any opinions on Eydis?
When [Stuck:he/she] finally comes free of the mud, [Laugher:Name] gives [Stuck:Name] a congratulatory pat on the back.
Acid Pot
But I cannot send my warriors to aid you.
When Caustantin falls, there will be no-one left to coordinate the defence of Perth. It's likely the army will break up by clan and scatter.
Can you pick one of them off from a distance?
The Pictish army is in position on the west side of town.
All trade for miles around goes through this harbour.
The little witch? She's a life-saver! I mean that quite literally, she's patched me up more than once. Better than new! Good to have that sort around.
Well, seeing as how you people have been behaving around here, I doubt you'll have much luck, but we'll escort you to Perth if you want to go there.
Look, it's pretty obvious you aren't merchants. I don't appreciate the dishonesty, so I think it's best if you leave.
Long enough that I'm used to it. It's gotten worse lately though.
He nods without hesitation.
Father has two totems that he lends to people when they need to represent him. If you show the totem to the guards, they'll let you right in.
Flew in on a dragon, actually.
What happened?
I certainly have. One does not easily forget a man like Gunnarr. You've met him too, I take it. Not in combat, I hope?
We're watching you. You and your gang better behave yourselves!
I think we both know that price is unconscionable.
What are you doing?

Grimulfr yes, but not your father. The ship had a skeleton crew, just five men led by Grimulfr. They mentioned that the ship belonged to a [Player:Father], but something had gone wrong and they were headed home.
Danr shouts over his shoulder.
I wish I could say I were surprised, but that's quite typical of the lies levelled at us by other communities within the Church.
We must seek political allies elsewhere. That great kingdom across the sea - with their support, we might resist these attempts to subjugate us.
All right. No use delaying it any further.
A shaft downward is exposed at the edge of the cave, the bottom nowhere to be seen. This is where the draft is coming from. It's wide enough to fit a person, at least for about as far as you can see.
The smith Kveldulfr has retreated to the familiar confines of his workshop, where he's engaged in an energetic discussion with his wife Dagheidr.
The hint of a smirk plays at the corner of Eanbald's lips.
From the moment news of your landing reached Eoforwic, I knew it would come down to this. Your people have brought nothing but death and destruction to this land.
Thank you Hulda. I'll see you again.
It was generous of you to do so. You could've easily killed the two of them. Couldn't you?

The silence is so thick you can cut it with a knife. Nefja, Sigridr, and Ljotr are exchanging looks with each other and yourself - it's not difficult to imagine the heated debates taking place within each of their minds.
Skule's smirk is impossible to miss. He's got you right where he wants you.
Why?
You fell for Scary Witch Girl! I can't [i]believe[/i] you fell for Scary Witch Girl. There weren't any love potions involved by any chance, were there?
Æthelred's hall is buzzing with activity, yet the King's men wave you through directly.
How could any man refuse you?
It takes several long, awkward moments before she manages to compose herself. Her eyes are puffy and bright as she looks at you again.
If the women take up arms, I expect the other thralls will just wait and see how things pan out, but if you end up fighting Erlingr by himself, they'll probably join in.
Pack It Up
I'm just passing through, do you know anything about this place?
Nefja's mother Bjørgdis comes out of the bedroom when she hears the door open. She looks tired.
Aye, that's right, you're not Christian. They say you worship ancient violent gods that thirst for retribution against the spreading light of Christ.
How about we try something slightly more tactical, big guy? I think I can pick one of them off from this distance to begin with.
The trader fixes you with a skeptical look.
Calm yourself, Erlingr. Don't try to pretend you haven't gotten yourself into this mess...
For the past year, I have negotiated the marriage between my son and the daughter of King Donncoirce of Dal Riata. Such a union will bring our kingdoms together for good.
This amulet is the only thing Ketill has to remember his sister by. It means a lot to him.
You notice a skinned deer that lies dead at the perimeter, some of its meat boiling in the pot.
No! Please! At least spare the women!
Two of your father's brothers went with him on his final expedition. Only Grimulfr returned. This helmet belonged to Sighialmr, the youngest of the three.
You made my husband poison Conall mac Taidg! [i]And then you simply left![/i]
Will you sell some of those drinks and remedies?
What about it?
They're here! Look!
I am an ally of Æthelred. I may be able to help.
{Give golden eagle standard.} Look what I brought home.
I'm... sure it was.
You spend some time tying together a rope that's long enough and fix it to a large stalagmite next to the shaft.
My boys saw it! You accurst Halfdansons think you can just...
The tanner reaches painfully behind him and - after a bit of rummaging - retrieves a small scrap of fabric in the colours of Osred's crest.
It's been worse than I thought.
The thieves are dead.
The smith grumbles, but he accepts the coins.
He responds with a half-nod, but then seems to think better of it.
Travel west to Dal Riata and Donncoirce's homestead and uncover what has happened. If she still lives, and God help us otherwise, bring the princess Finnguala back to Perth so she can marry my son.
No, I-- I was already robbed once today! How do you think... that I got into this mess!
{Kill the wounded buck.}
You [i]like[/i] me? Well excuse me if your words don't exactly cause me to swoon, seeing as how you're trying to take my land!
Pleasure to make your acquaintance.
{Attack.} Caustantin mac Fergusa sends his regards!
Just like [Player:Father], disrespectful even in the face of a challenge against your honour.
[i]My[/i] trap?! I was as surprised as you when the king ordered your arrest.
Better to die gloriously here than to live a long and boring life at home.
Her brows furrow in honest sympathy.
Then you are truly one of mine. At the end of your rope, we will meet again in my hall.
The crew of the other ship starts taking pot-shots at you as soon as they're within arrow range, and by a stroke of bad luck, one of the projectiles nails [Victim:Name] in the shoulder.
Your uncle Grimulfr taught you to fight with a two-handed axe, his favoured weapon. The first time you ever beat him at practice, he gave you this dane-axe as a symbol of your graduation.
{Paint a picture of a unified north under Caustantin, and Wada's very important place in it.}
Let me take a look at your wares.
The groom regards you with cloudy eyes, and his speech is noticeably slurred.
Must be the ones we killed earlier.
I've got nothing.
A small embroidered strip of cloth in the colours of Osred's family. It holds no value, but it clearly has some secret purpose.
If we wait until they stop expecting an attack and [i]then[/i] strike, we'll at least have a chance to reach Skule and end him before they can mobilise.
It'll be good for those girls to get a new man on the farm. It's not safe for them to live alone out there.
Fire and Steel
On second thought, I think there was something...
Four against one! This is what the sons of Erlingr Thorgislsson consider a fair fight?!
Let's find that godi first.
Of course we can do something! What if-- can you go to Hulda? Ask her if she has any more ideas. [i]Please[/i].
{Offer 80 Valuables.} You must've been standing here for quite some time. If I were to hand you four pence for an ale, I could make these sorry sods somebody else's problem.
He admits the village is to blame, but he refuses to do anything about it.
I've tilled a field or two, but I left that life behind.
A few minutes pass, and no sounds that could be construed as footsteps have sounded. The girl in your grip starts to quietly sob.
Well! What a surprise. More guests from across the seas! What are you called, friend?
Our clan has been so weak. Halfdanr helped me see how our father failed as a chieftain.
Please... I couldn't bear to lose him, knowing I was the one who...
You... you ask too much of me.
Y-yes?
His escape could create a useful distraction.
Aye so I've heard. I'd join you if I could, but you know how it is with my leg.
Aife grumbles under her breath.
I-- I'm sorry we couldn't help Eyfura, but I won't let her-- her death... I won't give up my dreams.
Here, take it, just don't hurt me!
She gives you a sarcastic snort, but then she seems to realise you were serious, and her look changes. For a moment, she looks at you in a very different way.
Return to Skjern and speak to Astridr to end your adventures in Britain.
Me too.
{Keep eating.} I feast... as my father does... in Valhøll.
I understand. Good luck, [Player:Name].
Congratulations on your return to power. I take it this seals our agreement?
This is worse than I could have imagined. Rurik under the sway of Skule. How could I have failed him so?
You and your family are traitors to the clan. I have come to kill you and your last son. The women will be exiled.
Of course. I - ah - hope the offer didn't offend. We've had very little contact with your people until now, and I know almost nothing about your culture.
You just realised you're outclassed, didn't you?
You won't live long enough to find out.
I'm certain father is feasting with Odinn now. The old man will surely be more at home in Valhøll than he ever was here.
Just planning ahead. You never know when a group of misguided outcasts will come in handy.
What are you selling?
Once the scavengers are dealt with, the young girl approaches you timidly.
Let's take another look around, just let me know when you're ready to make your decision.
Thanks, I'll leave you to your work.
Perhaps I'll return when I have something to pay you with.
Enough! No worse provision can man carry, than too deep a draught of ale. Let it be a draw!
The harbourmaster eyes your blade nervously.
I'm preparing to mount an expedition to the west.
Before you is a table laden with wooden platters of fruits, cheeses, and sweetmeats. Ingimarr stands at one end, biting into an apple and chewing with great relish.
Of course I remember. Don't give me that look, like I wouldn't remember.
Producing your seax, you carve a jagged piece of bark off the trunk around the patch, leaving no more mold on the great old tree.
I've got five people that need finding.
Rurik would never betray me like that!

Finally, the crowd disperses back into the camp and throughout the forest to loot the fallen, aid the wounded, and pack up the camp. It looks like an utterly disorganised process, yet within just four hours, the different parts of Æthelred's armies begin to form up and march south out of Yngilwood.
I've heard of you! You took control of Orkney recently, did you not?
I can't spare 200 ørtug of silver.
Dead?! But-- wait!
Don't touch that, please. That's my property.
My father was thegn before me. He met his end on these islands. There were other challengers, but I won the right to succeed him.
Why would I have? You seem like capable people. I have nothing to lose and everything to gain by enlisting your help!
If I were more like you, I could have stopped them.
You snivelling little shit! Come over here and say that again!
Bjørgdis pulls both of her daughters into a tight hug.
Fantastic.
In that case, I take back my objection.
We are here to seek allies in our struggles at home.
The young witch musters a half-smile.
You're damn right they're repaid, Viking! Now go! And God-speed!
They had taken to worship Romulus as a saint. The founder of Rome. Can you believe it?
You know... I would never judge someone for their inclinations.
That's too bad. Oh well, far vel.
Pretty good!
Thank you, I'll see you at the peak.
The farmer watches the murders wide-eyed from a safe distance. Momentarily overwhelmed by horror, he nearly drops the poison you gave him. Then he remembers himself and hurries over to the barrels.
I let you have that one, just to keep things interesting!
An involuntary laugh of joy bursts from the young man's lips.
But when the sun was up they were scorched, and because they had no root they withered away.
Now [i]here's[/i] someone who knows a thing or two about courage, lads. The monster-slayer [Player:himself/herself]!
I ran the thieves out of your buildings.
Nothing you do will make me betray my loyalty to Osred!
You sure you don't need anything? I'll be happy to make you something.
His teeth clench and he breathes heavily through his nose as you loom over him, but there is a measure of satisfaction on his face.
If only you'd see--!
[i]What[/i] an asshole.
I've never been better. For the first time in my life, I'm here because of my [i]own[/i] decisions.
Sure, take me across the river.
{Let them leave.} All right, you get on out of here then.
On some level I hope he will. He was a good ruler, in my view - not strong, but wise, and attentive to the needs of his people.
Nefja stands up and stretches with a yawn. A note of honey drips into her voice.
It's better than nothing. When we regain our strength, we may sail south to buy some livestock.
I think I'll just stick to the one free man, instead.
Of course.
I'm [i]glad[/i] you came here in person, Viking - I will make sure Grainne is avenged!
It was a very good deal for me, but it sounds like my old sword didn't serve him well in the end.

This expedition has been many months in the making, but the time for talk and deliberations is over. Out there, in the land across the sea, we will find great riches - and we will plunder every last bit of it!
I'm gonna end you!
You think I've done all of this for the applause? My hostility pushed you to become a great [Player:man/woman], but that's not the reason for any of my actions.
That's a harsh thing to say, and saying it now verges on cruelty. Even if you're right.
A deep frown settles across his brows.
Because I refuse to settle for the lesser of two evils.
My great-aunt has a farm not far from here. She'll help me.
I am no warrior. These things belonged to my beautiful wife, Vigundr.
Next time you show yourself to be so insolent, I will [i]not[/i] aim to only wound.
You carry yourself like a druid, and that's something. Hopefully it'll be enough. Will you let my servants show you to your new home, Cillian?
{Evaluate your surroundings.}
Don't leave me here! I'm so cold, so tired. I love you...
It's over quickly. You approach the three Northumbrians with a closed fist extended, then bring up your seax and thrust it three times into the chest of the younger of the men.
Leave.
Yeah, [i]thanks[/i] Danr, your contribution is appreciated.

It's no secret I didn't agree with how [Player:Father] ruled our clan. Bearing this in mind, I don't see what gives you the right to succeed him. But this feast is in his honour, and I will not insult his memory here, nor will I challenge your claim to leadership.
I knew it! These people are dirt-poor, we'll find no horses here.

With that, the blond warrior stalks back to camp to treat his new injury. The rest of your hird eventually seems to figure out what transpired, and their jokes at his expense show that they clearly believe you were in the right.
This sounds like not at all my problem.
The godi is preparing an ornate dagger as you come near.
You're here to kill him, right? Can't imagine your sort would turn up for anything less than murder for hire.
What terms do you have in mind?
Will you both accompany us to Perth?
Rurik places a hand gingerly on your shoulder. You can barely hear his soft voice over the din of the feast.
Rurik chuckles. You can barely hear his soft voice over the din of the feast.
And just why would we do that? This is our beach, not yours!
{Pay 1200 Valuables.} It's a deal.
Ottarr's brother Toste sneers. He sounds drunk.
Sure, thank you.
Grettir's Corpse
That's great, but what are you proposing?
Come on, we're done here.
We don't take kindly to such threats!
They took him. North. Bressal knows where.
Not this year, fortunately. It's been a very peaceful season for me. I'm just here to stay informed.
{Show him the ribbon from Willibrord.} Osred sent me to get a report from you.
Now I'm told they escaped over the winter. This puts me in a very precarious spot - my people will not be happy if they learn I took their money and then lost the goods.
Ethelyn, runaway wanted alive by her family. Last seen in the company of travelling bards travelling north towards Yngilwood. Reward: 1200 Valuables.
Just [i]what[/i] do you actually hope to achieve by attacking this wedding?
As she spends most of her days roaming the countryside, Sigridr tends to know what's happening in your lands better than anyone else.
Well that should be straight-forward, right? We find this Conall person, capture him, and bring him back here.
It's the way of all things to wither and die. No way around it.
You took this charred bone talisman from the arsonist Geirmundr Bare-leg, who had fled Ribe after starting a fire.
I'd rather not. It seems our presence here is unwanted.

If you were to drive out the outlaws and reunite the villagers with their possessions, they would have the means to give you what you're after - and what stronger demonstration of good-will could they wish for?
Nefja believes some kind of curse afflicts her family. She believes it caused the disease that killed her sister and may now have affected her mother as well.
And you'd be a maiden still, for sure!

[Drinker:Name] manages to finish two brimming cups before leaning forward with hands on [Drinker:his/her] knees. [Drinker:He/She] hiccups and looks for a moment as though [Drinker:he/she] is about to be sick.
A few of our allies appear to have broken through the lines.
The forge will be cooling soon.
Leofric bows before you. Despite everything, he still smiles.
Very well. I'll return when it's done.
He had better not give me cause to regret sparing him. It’s not too late to lob off his head.
How is [i]that thing we discussed[/i] coming along?
Leofric maintains his smile for a moment longer before he lets it drop. He looks most of all disappointed.
I can tell you're a reasonable sort. How about a deal, hm?
Tried, boys. Let no one say your mom didn't try.

It's clear that the feast has been a roaring success. Tableware is scattered around the house, those guests who aren't already passed out are still dancing and drinking, and nobody pays attention to the Vikings that just walked through the door.
It is inevitable that such missteps happen when new cultures meet. If my influence can prevent such a thing from happening again, I have a duty to stay.
Excavate
You send a few shots of your own in their direction, but then the crew of the other ships seems to finally get a good look at [Shipname] and lose their nerve.
[Buzzkill:Name] recoils and snarls.
The smell of sea is strong on the air, and the sound of a powerful surf battering the cliffs is heard as a great roar even from up here.
I could make it worth your while.
He was no match for me.
There is still time before Althing. The isles across the sea still have secrets left for us.
Defeat Ingimarr.
Kveldulfr, denying my request will not keep Asleifr safe, it will only put me in danger...
It was said that Loki tricked his blind half-brother Hodr into killing Baldr with an arrow made of Mistletoe, Baldr's only weakness.
The two kings embrace each other, then their children, then the priest, who looks a little taken aback by the sudden lapse of formalities.
A pile of animal pelts, from sheep and a few deer, lie conspicuously stacked in the small clearing. A gamey, decayed smell wafts about the area.
I'm glad you came. I couldn't make the swim back so I decided to wait here.
Eydis gives you a wry smile.
His jaw literally drops.
One of your own kind, I don't remember her name - it sounded like a throaty death-rattle. She was a dark-haired warrior woman with a sinister disposition.

I should have never-- trusted you. You're the worst thing that ever-- ever happened to me. Curse you! And curse me... for being so [i]stupid[/i].

I haven't gone anywhere.

You rush the lone monk and swing heavily, but he manages to step aside, and you catch a glimpse of steel in his hand. Out of pure instinct, you draw your seax and drive it into his heart before he has time to slash.
What did you find? Was the treasure there? Did you meet the Underground Ones?
Talk to Wada about his plan to gain the bishop's support.

Nefja Holmunardottir has volunteered to fight in the place of [Player:Name]. I fight for myself.
I know you only want what's best for me, but you don't understand what it's like. I need this.
Doesn't matter. We're here for [i]all[/i] of you. You're dangerous, and we should've dealt with you as soon as you showed up!
A tiny wrinkle of the nose is the only sign that Eydis even registers the smell.
Enough playing around. Here's what I believe happened...
When this is over I will shower you in gold!
I'll consider your request.
I assume Odinn decided on a whim to grant me complete power over language just now. Why would I lie?
We should get out of here.
Grettir squints at you for a long moment. He shrugs and takes a few steps back.
What happened here?
This is [Player:Name]. The [Player:son/daughter] of [Player:Father] and Astridr. Do you remember [Player:him/her]?
No shit?
Vengeance will be mine!
The chamber holds a weapon that once belonged to a great Roman hero. So I was told. If you find it - it's yours.
Oh God... such senseless slaughter! Oh good Lord save the souls of my brave subjects!
I'll meet you atop the mountain, I have to pack my last things. Now go! Aid him!
Willibrord screams in agony. He won't be doing any tanning with that hand any time soon.
I couldn't just leave you to your fates.
{Keep going.}
I tried, but by heart just wasn't in it. Preferred sailing, fighting... pillaging.
What is your relationship to the thegn Skule Skullcleaver?
The rest of the hird is over there.
Treasure! We should dig it up. Who knows what else could be down there!
I like to say that I'm driven by crippling feelings of inferiority tempered by overpowering megalomania.
Recruit at least nine hirdmen for your expedition.
I missed, that's all.
For this to work, you'll need to distract them while I tamper with the ale.
The witch makes me uneasy. I do not know what dark powers she consorts with. But she knows how to treat a wound, so I see your wisdom in bringing her along.
[Curious01:Name] looks even more worried. [Curious01:His/Her] eyes search for the exit.

One of the new arrivals appears to be a smith, a lean woman with strong arms who (you presume) has singlehandedly finished the half-constructed house that stood here before and turned it into her smithy.
Go jump off a cliff.
I don't know! A lot! Why?
You'll do as I say, or I will kill you. It really is as simple as that.
A solitary thrall has put down his axe to watch the fighting from a safe distance. The glow of the blazing farmhouse casts him in an orange hue.
Go north from here until you reach Grimulfr's cottage, then take the far path east into the forest.
Well, see... I'm not so much leaving you a choice here. Understand?
That should be clear enough for us to find the place.
Beod ge gesund travellers. May the faerie guide you on your path.
Sure does. Are you gonna take me up on it?
Considering the way people speak of you, like you're a true hero of Perth, I'll give you the very best prices I'm able. Let me take a look.
We came here because we had no other option.
The unseen nun on the other side adopts the tone of an elder scolding a child.
I'd like to look at your goods, Uallach.
Cease your complaints. Look! They're bringing in the food.
Passing right through our camp.
Nefja blushes slightly.
[Player:Name], I volunteer to fight in your place.
Is that a threat? Do you hope to menace me into submission?
[Archer:Name] leans out to take a look.
{Reject her offer.} Not a chance.
Hello again [Player:lad/lass]. Have you scrounged up some silver, yet?
Poor Ulfr. He survived such dangers, only to be struck down in his own home. He could have been a great help to train the young while you're away.
Good to know.
{Offer 1000 Valuables.} I'll pay you 50 pence if you tell me who this was made for.
Merchants carry stories of our wealth throughout the country. We've even started buying up more of the surrounding land, to expand our influence.
Looks like there's plenty of mushrooms right here.
A good deal for both of us I think. Will that be all?
Carnwennan
Let's hope you won't need it, hm?
{Offer 200 Valuables.} Would ten pence convince you to leave your post for a few minutes?
Stand aside, or draw your weapon. Either way works for us.
Leofric himself finds you deep inside the cave.

Sorry, we uh, don't want any trouble. Ask away.
That old hag in the bog over there even sold me a few tinctures of medicine! I'm sure you'll find my stall well stocked.
And how do you prove yourself worthy?
How can you say that, Sig?! We've all known him since he was a little boy!
Her face flushes and she cups her reddening cheeks.
He smiles, but there's a shrewd gleam in his eyes.
Spare... the women. I beg you...
If you play your cards right, you may end up the new ruler of Eoforwic. I would give it to you up front for your service, but there are many political concerns to be accounted for.
Enough! You may be the thegn, but you're still my [Player:nephew/niece]! Let an old man keep some secrets, for the sake of his own grief.
Maybe, if a chance comes up.
The hunter wipes mud out of his eye.
{Attack Oddkell and his disciples.} I've made my choice, yes.
It's my right! I'm the eldest son! I've been running from that responsibility for my entire life. It's time I face who I am.
The deed is done. Time to return to the village.
Where have you hidden the valuables? Hm?!
The others are wrong. I'm your [Player:brother/sister], and I know your strength. The strength of your wisdom and your kindness.
Nothing! I know nothing! We never made it past Orkneyjar before Gunnarr's change of heart.
Perth lays far to the north, in the wild Pictish lands. Some of the Picts still cling to their old faith, and I hope to meet with them and chronicle their stories.
I'm glad you two finally hooked up. He's been throwing meaningful glances at you for years, I think he was [i]this[/i] close to serenading your tent! Thank the gods you averted that disaster.

I don't plan to leave empty-handed.
[i]Two[/i] witches.

[Random01:Name] raises a single eyebrow.
Tell them to throw down their weapons or we'll teach them a lesson they won't soon forget.
Have you now? They are of little interest to anyone but the Northmen, who can reach them in just a few weeks at sea.
Why don't you talk to the smith inside the walls? When you know what's needed, my stall will still be here, and I'm all too happy to sell you the materials for the smith's work.

The gods do not favour the cautious, so today we seize our own fate. Just as each of us will ultimately travel alone to Valhøll, we must all find the strength within ourselves to face whatever dangers await us.
Fix things for father. Help little brother.
Josteinn shakes his head and chuckles.

A small smile plays across her lips every time her hammer strikes the anvil, and when you approach, she sighs contentedly and wipes the sweat from her brow.
You will fill this place with the ghosts of innocents. That is the price you pay to be remembered.
There's one thing I've been meaning to say. I was really rude when we met in Ribe, and I feel super bad about that.
To take you to Perth, where you'll serve as religious advisor to the king.
The king sighs heavily.
When I grow up I want to be a Viking too. Where have you gone?
Down the narrow passage between houses, a small group of young warriors are gathered around a fire. With a start, you recognise Skule's scouts from Skjern forest.
I share your surprise, to put it lightly. Why are you here?
Steinn looks like he's fully recovered from having his heart torn out. He paces back and forth in front of his hird, feeling the weight of the shield in his hand.
What good could possibly come from the fire which tore through the poor district?
There. You'll be all right. Do you need anything else?
We should have stayed on Orkneyjar. We had a good thing going there... and the painted ones couldn't have kept us at bay for long.
You are a fool. Terrible things befall those who defy the Underground Ones.
I agree - delaying is not without risks. But if you're confident we'll get there in time, I defer to your judgment.
You have at last achieved what you set out to do. The British Isles may still hold opportunities for you, but the day of the Althing is approaching, and you must attend.
King Donncoirce, we're here to rescue you.
I can tell you already have new matters on your mind. If you'll have one of your subjects show me to my new home, I'll give you peace to talk.
He looks up from his feet, his eyes searching for something in your face. Then his chin rises as though raised by an invisible hand.
It'll be a shame to kill her, but letting her live is more trouble than she's worth.

You signal for [Archer:Name] to follow you, and the two of you quietly take up positions at the top of the earth ramp. You take aim together and loose simultaneously. Both your targets drop without a sound.
I'll see you around.
Caustantin seems to trust you, so I trust you too, and my prices will reflect it. Let me take a look.
We'll win! We've no choice! That bark is my boy's only chance!
I accept.
Josteinn holds up a hand in salute as he runs past you.
We could all be at home right now, playing with our children, helping our wives, and tending to the farms.
Sling-stone
What did you...?
{Search for Ketill.}
It was gracious of you to spare Asleifr, but I understand why you could not let him stay.
It was about time Sigurdr Hringr acknowledged your status as Jarl.
That must've hurt.
[Eater:He/She] reaches for a slab of salted oxtongue and tears into it with [Eater:his/her] bared teeth. The air fills with grunts, coughs and the smacking of lips as the two set about their task.
That's a fine spear. These guys must be well trained.
We'll start with the town of Dun Phris. A conflict between our kingdoms has long simmered there.
Very well then, we'll see who is the strongest of us - but let's not fight here, on the beach. Come, follow me.
Ask Eydis about that grave site she used to tell stories about.
The gods will surely grant you their favour. Take this talisman as a symbol of your devotion.
Exotic Necklace
I know a good place for the ambush. This way.
Wes hal! I assume you came here to violate the holy ground you are standing on with my blood?
If you need a place to stay while you prepare for a longer journey, you are welcome to camp here. But tell me, why have you brought your ship to my beach?
You have my word, on the honour of my family, and as the past and future king of Northumbria. I will be your ally for as long as I sit on the throne.
On the contrary, your hospitality is appreciated.
Here, please accept this as token of my gratitude.
He and his crew attacked my clan. We fought him and won, and I offered to spare him for his service.
With all this trouble we've had lately, nobody has had time to go out and get more medicine for her.
Thank you for your courage. We have so little, I couldn't bear to lose the last of my grandfather's old figurines.
You go over the plan, outlining the contributions and the risks associated with each person's part in it, making sure to play up how integral each member of your hird will be.
That is... something. But still you stole from them. You ransacked God's house, and you took the fruits of their labour.
Lifesucker
I hear you. I can't wait to see what awaits us over there.
Asleifr gives you a withering look.
It was closer than I would've liked. The people of Skjern fought better than expected.
Most of the others have gone to bed, but Ketill is still sitting up at the fire in deep thought, poking the embers with the head of an arrow. He looks up when he hears you and beckons you closer.
I believe you.
So?
Oh come off it, this mix-up isn't our fault. I don't want to fight you over this, but we sure aren't handing it over either.
As you withdraw your blade from the poet's intestines, he stumbles to the ground with a comically sheepish look on his face.
To make a cure, the gydja in Ribe needs bark from the Troll Tree in the marsh.
Your defences are weak! No palisades, the barest excuse for earthworks. You're a tempting target!
She looks up at Asleifr with a gleam in her eyes.
You clean the wound with water and then fetch the dried cow piss to disinfect. You can feel her tense up as you apply the ointment, but she doesn't make a sound.
Tell us where to find treasure!
Ciamar a tha sibh?
It's now or never.
Find a survivor of the fire.
If I have one less scout to pay at the end of this war, that's thirty pence I can offer [i]you[/i] instead.
I'm not to blame for that.
We'll be there if we must.
I'm told you have a plan to attack Pictavia.
She gestures towards the opposite side of the market.
I've got you.
That huntress of yours, Sigridr, sold me some well-skinned pelts, and a smith in the next village over sold me a small selection of metal scraps.
A challenge then! Like Thorr in Utgardr!
Though Gunnarr was defeated, the damage to the reputation and security of Skjern is done. Sigurdr Hringr will side with us at the Althing.
A wise choice! Will you stay at least for moral support?
Thegn [Player:Name]! I can't believe you're just giving us this place. It's a whole farm!
I'm relieved to hear that. What can I do to serve?
Better get the hearth fired well. It'll be a cold night again.
A sorry-looking man sits on the boardwalk, a small selection of equipment spread out on a wool blanket in front of him.
Truly the gods favour us! Such a weight off all our shoulders.
Aiblinn extends her hand and shakes on it. She is tired, and her grip is weak, but her gaze is no less fierce for it.
Tell me, what are your plans for this place? How will you lead your clan?
[Lover:Name] shoots you a very significant look.
I wish my head had been clear.
Adopting the tone and manners of an old monk lecturing a group of initiates, Morcant explains what the stones revealed.
Do you know where we might find her?
She throws you a small pouch.
Damn right he did! And it seems I should count myself lucky to be working with you instead of your rival.

Your eminence, I am honoured to host you in my hall.
I'd heard [Player:Father] had neglected his clan for years, but this is just sad.
The dead body of Rikvi, a young woman from Skerninge who had eloped with a caravan guard.
I was the one who had her poison you. If you're still angry about it, be angry at [i]me[/i].
Dubglas throws up his arms. The desperation is his voice is clear.
The [Shipname] is a beautiful ship.

Welcome back to my humble stall, Norsemen. People say you've been doing your best to make up for the... [i]questionable[/i] reputation of your people. For your efforts, I'll give you a good deal if you're looking to buy.
I agree. If we do decide to exploit this chance, Skallagrimr in Orkneyjar needs to know. The decision is yours.
We should care of these sentries before they realise we're here.
The young boy resembles the spy you interrogated at Æthelred's camp. These kids must be his children, imprisoned for leverage against him.
He gives you a grim look.
You are astute, my Northern friend.
The smith crosses his massive arms and shakes his head.
At first they exchange confused glances, but then the young hunters seem to realise you mean it.
The difference may be academic - heathenry is just one of many disguises worn by the Adversary. I hope these people occupy Legacæstir no more?
Grimr has been released from my service. He serves you now - the Jarl of Orkneyjar.
Please forgive my deception. Is there nothing else we can do to gain your favour?
She spins around and picks up her clothes, pulling it back on almost frantically. She's sniffling as she blows out the candles.
You promised to tell me something about your own religion.
Quiet, girl!
It was just a thought.
Quit your bickering, we need to think.
You flatter me, Kyre. Yet I feel undone in your presence.
He nods again.
Now Æthelred is all that stands between you and Northumbria's throne. You put him on that throne, and I'm certain you can just as easily take it away from him.

Mind your own damn business.
Tell me about the Mardollsons.

Myrddin lifts his head to reward you with a grateful smile.

Why don't you cross the river?
I hear you showed mercy to their king. You knew him better than I, so I will not judge if that was right or wrong. He may be trouble for us in the future. Then again he may be of use.
I hope you won't hold this against me, but I'm freeing your thralls!
White Glove
Gunnarr is still where you left him. A hog is curiously sniffing his pants.
Then you are not entirely without mercy. Thank you.
Perhaps one of the traders at the market will be able to handle it for us.
That was... educational.
Well said. There's no telling what we'll find over there, but with me as your bannerman, you have nothing to fear.
How we suffer for Skjern's honour.
