Beo gesund, my Mysterious Stranger. May the faerie guide you on your path.
I am not Northumbrian. I am Norse, sent here by Osred as a neutral party.
I'm glad to hear it. You sure know how to brew mead up there in Skjern! Drink that good is dangerous - but it's a danger I gladly face.
Skakki was working with Conall before we got to him. It seems like Skule may have attempted a similar alliance, but he chose the wrong king to support.
It is the north wind that lashes men into vikings!
He straightens his back, and his voice rolls like thunder from an oncoming storm cloud.
A group of Christians are hunting disbelievers seeking sanctuary in the old Roman fortress in Legacæstir.
Show yourself, or face the tip of my sword!
Put that down! That's ours!
Far vel.
Your bearing betrays a strength that rivals any man. I think you must be an avatar of the goddess Sif.
If you will accept help from a witch's apprentice, I may have something you can use.
I've fastened the rope over there. The log is well concealed among the branches overhead, but try to keep Asleifr's attention on you when he comes.
That's far enough!
Godan dag.
The king has hired you? Hm. I guess I see the reason in that.
She regards you with eyes that are free of all suspicion.
Sounds complicated, let's just beat these people and take what we came for.
Grainne squeezes her eyes shut in anger and pain, but she says nothing.
Aldwine lives there, down the lane. I beg, put the fear of God in him.
{Knock her out.}
Reminisce over a horn of mead.
He will see his day before the court soon enough. Had he not fled, the sentence would have been lenient. Now... I doubt it. 55 pence for bringing him in alive.
Asleifr mutters disdainfully.
Valerius is engaged in some discussion with his disciples. When he sees you, he looks up and smiles.
Skallagrimr grins, excited.

We are not raiders setting out to pillage and steal. Across the sea, we will find a great kingdom. We will secure an alliance with their king and return here with such might that no one will ever dare to strike at us again.
Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.
Uhm--
Until I see his body, he's alive! Do you understand?
[Lover:Name] appears to have already risen and left your tent to start the morning's chores.
A learned man's heart whose learning is deep, seldom sings with joy.
We still have time. The trip takes no more than a week.
{Travel to Perth.}
Wes hal. Name's Cuthrad, can I help you?
All right, I'll find your druid.
I see. Well, [Player:he/she] will be too late. Hlunnbjørn is well on its way.
Indeed. We want to gain entry.
It would certainly be an easy way to dispose of the cultists within the tunnels. Not necessarily an admirable solution though, and it doesn't solve the problem posed by those aboveground.
Oh Aedan's quick to anger, but just as quick to come out of it. Dub's choice to step in calmed him down.
They were going to head east out of the highlands to meet with some of those Norsemen.
Myrddin...?
Hidden Stash
Spare Cailtram mac Muircholaig if you encounter him.
I'm not sure.
I have you right where I want you!
We had a deal with the other thegn, your neighbour to the north. He told his watchmen not to light their beacons if they saw our sail.
The man who appears to be the head praetorian bangs the end of his spear against the tiles.
What do you propose we do then?
I talked to him. He'll be leaving soon.
A wise course. I can already tell you will make a better thegn than [Player:Father]. As I said, he was a great warrior - but it's clear that's where his interests lay.
In the back, you notice a familiar face: Aife has rejoined her original mistress.
Meanwhile, you and your hird can sail [Shipname] all the way into the heart of the city.
One of Osred's tax collectors by the name of Waltheof has absconded. His trial is guaranteed to end with a considerable fine for all the taxes he has failed to produce.
Is your family not here?
Ketill chuckles, but then a pensive looks comes over him.
We'll ambush Osred's delegation on the west road. Then we'll approach the Mercians and offer them great riches to support our own invasion of Northumbria.

Valkyrie's Flower

We're here to visit the burial mound.

A group of peasants have assembled to defend the outer farms from those of your allies who have made it through the outer defences. They look underequipped and unconfident, but there are a lot of them.

I stumbled! It went over the wall and then... I went to go get it before father came home.

I don't have time to jerk around. What do you need?

You'd estimate her age to be in the early 20's. Green eyes gleam under dark bangs. She is short, with a healthy plump build, and her skin is smooth and pale. Her dainty hands rest on her hips - within quick reach of her knife's hilt.
I'm looking forward to it. It's been a while since my warriors and I found challenge in combat.
Why on Earth would you let the spy escape? What guarantee do you have that they won't tell Osred everything?
A man in blue attacked us. He stole a figurine.
Remember - we need him alive. He has to tell us who he's meeting.
When she's done, she sits for a while beside you, feeling the warmth of the crackling fire. Then she gets up to grab some food as well.
Yeah.

Northumbria quickly moved to secure the most convenient passages through Hadrian's Wall.
I'm almost looking forward to killing that honourless piece of shit.
The giant shrugs, a motion not unlike an oak bending in a gale.
Did Fliri steal the pig?
Nothing! Nothing can make us leave!
Some unusual mixture of sadness and relief washes over him. He holds your gaze for a long moment, then he seems to get back some of the energy the duel took out of him, and he stands.
Once free of the shaft, you drop a short distance to the ground below and realise that you'll have to find another way out without a rope.

You attempt to swallow but the bite won't go down. Instead, you feel a heaving sensation as your gut clenches. Only just managing to twist away from the table, a spray of sour bile and masticated food spill from your mouth. You retch and heave for seveal agonizing moments.
Fine. We accept.
A sick grin distorts his face.
What is the value of an oath to a godless heathen?!
What'll I do now?
Eydis laughs warmly.
Fortress? It's a place of peace... of worship...
All is quiet in the cave when you come to. You find [Random01:Name] kneeling next to the druid. [Random01:He/She] looks up and meets your gaze.
Let's not get carried away by fanciful stories of unprotected coasts full of treasure. I won't make the same mistake as my father.
I'm certain he is - Odinn would have to be a fool not to accept a warrior like him.
The giant looks astounded.

You have nothing to fear. [Guard:Name] is on watch.
Eydis is already tossing sacks of supplies onto the beach, making ready to establish a camp.
My thoughts as well! I will not stake my son's life on that!
Your challenger extends a hand towards you.
"Heart" is not a thing a true leader concerns himself with. Leave such frivolousness to the skalds.

Come off it, Morcant, they're all still alive.
The threat of his sorceries seems to have diminished. The monks debate how best to deal with him. As for you, your reward.
Turn the ship around!
Your clan's prosperity is substantially better off than when I first arrived. I think you'll find my prices quite fair now.

And I you.

A tall warrior stands surrounded by his warriors, sword and shield in hand and a look of steely determination on his face.
The sentry immediately stands aside to let you pass and bows respectfully.

Cynferd is sitting on the steps of the old shrine, reading a beautifully illuminated copy of the Bible. It's an enormous book - if he lugs that around everywhere he goes, no wonder he's in good shape.
Eoforwic's walls and Leofric's command of them makes that city a dangerous prospect to attack.
You pull away from Ketill and go to your tent. He's staring after you with a flabbergasted expression.
So you've heard what happens to those who oppose me - how do you think you yourselves will fare if you stand in my way?
She shrugs, feigning apathy, but you can tell she's annoyed.
Will His Grace be held responsible if the seal is lost while in his care?
Let's talk about what kind of equipment you can make.
If Iovita's staying, [i]I'm[/i] staying.
{Help her get out of the armour.}
Well, this is... certainly an experience. I suspect we shall encounter guards soon. We should decide who will lead us if combat is unavoidable.
They're all dead. Your daughter has been avenged.
Out here in his new home, away from the big city, Jumper looks a little bit more his age.

I am [Player:Name], [Player:son/daughter] of [Player:Father].

She masks her feelings with a facial expression so blank it must be a facade.
Have you seen King Donncoirce?

Dead.

[Player:Name].

A simple silver cross with little ornamentation.
Quickest way to Hedeby, friend. I wanted to leave Ribe behind as quickly as possible.

Hello again. You're in luck: my contacts in Geatland have sent word they've captured new thralls.

The Calling of the Sea

Sigridr's mother fixes you with an evaluating look.

Next to you, all others are like candles next to the sun.
I will not cheat!
Yes
Seen them myself, your majesty. Five hundred men in Osred's colours, another two hundred in the colours of Mercia.

Kill the non-Christian refugees to enlist their persecutors.
My friends and I are yours to command for as long as the satanists remain.

Find out how the man died.

Later, we'll probably all be dead!

Goda nott.

You ask him to piss in the corner of a barrel! Hah!
That one too.
Then we were in Hulda's bog, and it was night but there was this weird red light, and I saw mom. She was holding Eyfura's hands and crying.
Find all the standing stones and uncover their secrets.

Breach Gate

I'm afraid King Sigurdr is preoccupied. He must ensure the full support of his thegns against any future Frankish incursions - I'm sure you understand: if Charlemagne attacks, we will be the first line of defence. The King has our best interests in mind.

Let me look at your wares.

It is done.

{Release her.} Ah, forget it.

She scratches her wrist.
You find Myrddin sitting crosslegged on the edge of his wood platform, slowly roasting some manner of herb above a candle.
You'll see we're in the right here.
So if I solve this for you, you'll give your support to Æthelred, so he'll give his support to me. Fantastic.
Hmm. Then we must be on our guard. He may get another chance to strike at us.
I'm sorry. This was really stupid. I just thought...
I considered him as near to a friend as our differences permitted. I couldn’t kill him.
Except you're not Christian, are you? They say you worship ancient gods that fight against the spreading light of Christ and compel you to seek violent deaths.
Six guards in front of [Player:Name]'s cell. Lightly armed.
Outside the tent, the reassuring sounds of your hirdmen going about their chores penetrate the silence of the camp.

Right!
Thank you.
Enough! Guards, to your king! Leave no Vikings alive!

Your brother holds your gaze for a moment, then he lets out a long breath.
Let's see if we can find another way around.
The young woman now looks mightily confused.
You put on your sympathetic face and paint a picture for Valerius - a picture of how unpopular he and his followers are around these parts, and how rapidly fear is spreading among the locals.
Erlingr has been exiled from the clan. Time to return to the village.
Our longships give us a great advantage in this war - both Perth and Eoforwic are built on rivers we can easily navigate.

A few tense minutes pass. The guarded looks crackling between your hird and the natives, and the uneasy shuffling of feet on both sides contrast bizarrely with the calm waves against the beach and the pretty songs of the birds among the trees.
Surely we're not going to dig up all the graves...?
Maybe we were wrong to come here, but here we are. We have to focus on the future of our clan.
Cillian...
The man's young wife screams in horror as her husband dies. The priestess pulls her into a hug and tries to shield her eyes.
Let's talk about putting that hammer of yours to use on some new work.
He grabs the seal out of your hand the second he sees it.
We only wish to pay our respects to the druid, as the highest leader of your traditional faith - one that is closely related to ours.
Found him skulking back toward the camp. His pockets are lined with silver coins.
Does that big guy have a dead goat strapped to his face?
Yer gonna have to do better than that!
The king in question grunts in mild annoyance.
An older, plump woman bears down on the boy with a severe frown.
That could be anywhere! Although the markings do seem to centre around the hunter's home. Hmm.
I will aid you!
Disfigurer
How could you possibly understand these people?
Very good. Come back any time.
I don't like to offend the gods in such a way.
You must learn to live with the shame.
I don't know what you're talking about.
{Stab the guard to death.}
Shit!
I'm sorry, kid. We tried to save him.
Why did you pass through here back then?
You did what you had to.
Another one of these strange stones. How many could there be?

This stone extolls the virtues of a warrior of great deeds who was a close friend of the mythical King of Albion. He was slain in battle when he was thrown off a cliff, and he was buried where he landed. Since then, a plethora of healing herbs and mushrooms always grow around his grave.
We can at least chop it up for the wood.
It was a pleasure to finally beat Grainne.
Danr continues unbothered as though there were no interruption.
Behold, a sower went to sow. And as he sowed, some seed fell by the wayside; and the birds came and devoured them.
That's a score we'll have to settle later. I was just on my way to tell you that the cult is gone from Legacæstir.
It's a powder. If he ingests this in the morning, he'll barely be able to stand at noon.
Come spring, my boys'll show you how to till and sow. Won't have to steal anymore.
We were set up by an old enemy. The shieldmaiden Hrodgærda has followed us to these shores.
They must have posted scouts atop the cliffs in advance. If you plan any kind of ruse, we'll need to take care of them first.
You shake on it, and the woman turns to one of her sons.
He nods heavily.
Shame.

Something catches your eye on the rim of the horn - a thin, clear paste smeared cunningly around the inside. You bring the vessel to your nose and smell, picking up a hint of grassy rhubarb alongside the strong scent of honey.
Uhm, I didn't mean it that way. You [i]are[/i] a great warrior, don't mistake me for thinking otherwise.
We seek the last of the druids. We're told he resides in this ravine.
What are your feelings on Morcant?
The Hlafdia asked me to give you this, with her thanks. She was... [i]very[/i] grateful.
I appreciate that. You'll learn all in due time.
Keep it to yourself or we'll kill you.
Thegn [Player:Name] and [Player:his/her] huscarls made a heroic effort to fend off the attackers, but the raid was successful. This episode has exposed serious flaws in the security of the region.
So be it. But this better be the end of it!
Are you not missing Ribe?
I'm surprised you let me off the boat. The way you and I get along, I wouldn't blame you for keeping me tied to the mast, HAH!
Where do they keep it? Do you know?
He begins to speak, and immediately breaks into a fit of deep throaty coughs. When he recovers, his voice is a rasp with an undertone of fear.
Thank you, kind thegn. Might you be interested in anything else?
Or the quiet times. The laughs around the campfire.
Be silent you drunken fool! We're just here to extend our congratulations... and take everything that you own!
What's the matter?
We should question the old man, see if he can at least point us in the right direction.
I come straight from Caustantin's hall. We've agreed to work for your king for the time being, but we need the [Shipname] to serve him best.
There is some muttering among the ranks, but the self-appointed leader of the farmers stands firm.
For a moment her facade of detached amusement drops, revealing genuine anger.
Spite us all you want, there's over a dozen of them, and those beasts are dangerous.
All right, if you put it that way...

The dowager Kyre in Eoforwic has bestowed tokens of her love on three of her past suitors, but each has abandoned her in turn. Kyre has asked you to retrieve the favours for her, promising a far greater reward for your help.
Oh, I found them all right. And I found their dead friend.
I'm feeling a bit thirsty, and there is plenty of ale.
You decide to give him some more time before you get worried. Hours pass and it's starting to get quite cold. Ketill remains absent.
Know this symbol...
You're right. Let's kick their ass.
So: what are you after?

You stop your horses on the outskirts of Erlingr Thorgislsson's homestead. Smoke rises lazily from the roof of the largest building. Thralls are going about their business in the fields. So far, it looks like nobody has noticed your arrival.
You walk for a long time, slow and careful to look for traces of Ketill. Finally, at the edge of the forest, the light of your torch reflects off something wet: blood spattered across rocks.
I... suppose.
Very well. Then let me look at that equipment.
The king spares Wada a brief annoyed glance.
He bangs his weapon against his second shield and gives you a sombre nod.
It's a privilege to be here your majesty.
We could have had great adventures, you and I. So what if I attacked your town - HAH! That's life! With me by your side, we would have been unstoppable.
Watch your tone, farmer.
Where are you headed?
No [i]-hck-[/i] no more... I give...
That seems to impress him.
Well a little water won't help us free [Player:Name]. Let's keep looking.
Thanks, that's gonna leave an impressive scar.

Her facade of courage nearly falters when you draw your seax. Her arms flail and twist as though grasping for any nearby handhold, until she finds your arm and grips it tightly while she draws her last breath.
Then they threw my husband on the fire! To burn alive! He screamed as he died - for your life! For [i]justice![/i]

Donncoirce arrived just in the nick of time, causing a slight delay while the horses of his retinue were stabled. He cried when he walked Finnguala into the hall, and the occasional sob still escapes him during Caustantin's speech.

The stone looks like it's stood here forever - its base is covered in lichen, its top in bird droppings. Strange markings are chiseled across its surface - some look like the shapes of animals or plants, but most are completely incomprehensible.
She snorts derisively.
Don't get me wrong, you'll only succeed in getting yourselves killed, but I'll be happy if you prove me wrong. These swine have stayed here for almost a fortnight.
There's no honour in this... I call your bluff, Ingimarr.
No children have ever been lost from the village, mind you, they're just trying to scare the wee ones to stay away from him.
Have you chosen your sacrifice?
Hurry and call the lads. We'll handle this.
What? Why? It's worthless to anyone but me!
That's your right of course. You are not a subject of mine. You've already done much for me, and you owe me nothing more.
Ingimarr's hand darts forth with suprising swiftness as he grabs your wrist.
Our work here isn't done yet!
His smile gives way to an expression of sadness.
Njord smile on us as we make ready to set sail.
{Evaluate your surroundings.}
Please come back if you change your mind.
Thank you! Oh, thank you. At last I can afford the journey home.
Have you seen a small group of people, two men and four women with children?
Røskva glides towards you like a mist, and your lips meet in a moment that stretches out around you in all directions.
I was sure there were enemies in the camp.
I wasn't planning to make you my bannerman.
An excited murmur rises among the guests. Ketill mutters in a voice too low for anyone other than you and Nefja to hear.
The druids are dead, to the best of my knowledge.
His gaze is vacant in a way that makes you think you might have given him any reason, and his answer would be the same.
I killed your sisters.
[i]Fuck.[/i]
His legs attempt to backpedal instinctively and he just barely avoids tripping over them, stumbling to a halt in front of you.
Men don't usually [i]run[/i] at the sight of me. Normally they just back away carefully.
Always a pleasure to serve a friend of King Caustantin. I'll give you my best prices.
{Nod.}
Regardless of the life you were born to, your culture shapes you. Had you been a chieftain in a Christian country, you would not be a warrior.
Nefja drops back into her fighting stance and levels Asleifr with a gaze that could make an oak wither.
Well that was rousing! What a bunch of cowardly cesspool-hogs, to come at you during a funeral. But! As they say... it's not a good feast until there's a fight!
Look at this, brothers!
The polite facade gains a subtle stiffness.
All right, don't go anywhere, we'll be back.
Tara freezes for a second, startled.
Outside, the sounds of music and merry chatter rise steadily, while - unknown to the festive Picts - a dozen longships enter the mouth of the River Tay.
Let's see if anyone nearby keeps dogs then.
Well, we're off to a poor start then, but that just means we've plenty of room to improve relations.
Jarl Ragnhildr smiles conspiratorially.
How?
Splendid. Truly splendid.
This town goes on forever...
So we're doing all the hard work.
It's a forge - by the look of your weapons, you should know that much. Now leave me to my work.
The Halfdansons and the Mardolsons
Those fires there... you can still smell the smoke on them.
She pauses a moment to enjoy the looks on some of your hirdmen's faces, then she giggles like a little girl.
Shame. Lost most of our lads when they took the king's penny to fight the wild men. Pox took the rest.
Could we find a translator somewhere? What sort of person would even know our language in addition to whatever these people speak?
That's what father never realised, isn't it? He always saw the physical weakness in people, but there are other kinds of strength.
Again his eyes scan you appraisingly.
The local priest claims you sacrifice people.
Don't just [i]stand[/i] there! KILL THEM!
Look at their shields and garb, [Player:Name]. These are Skule's men.
I don't deserve to live. I have failed my King, my duty, and my honour. Killing me would be a mercy.
He hooks his thumbs in his belt and sways back and forth on the soals of his feet.
The pass south of Perth is clear of Pictish warriors, their trap foiled before it could be sprung. The path to Perth lies open to Æthelred's army.
You're not much help, are you? Rest here tonight, but make sure you're gone by dawn.
Why are you selling your equipment?
Our walls are quite the sight, aren't they? They've stood for a thousand years as a symbol of the might and the order of the Roman empire!
I accept.
His nostrils flare, but he quickly reins it in. His eyes seek the ground.
Return to Perth and introduce Myrddin to Caustantin.
The large man looks shocked.
Well he's not gonna find out now, is he?
Ancient Tablet
She stands as you stand, and quickly close the distance, pressing her warm body against you.
{Drink the liquid.} Oh, fuck it.
Wilcume again! How may I assist you?
Wait! Please... don't go. Will you not stay with me tonight?
I suggest you leave the way you came. We don't like your kind around here.
Cuthrad looks you over, then looks to the other two, which both nod their heads.
{Weird growl.}
My parents are dead. They were killed in some stupid feud many years ago.
I was told to give this to a scout who worships the old gods alongside the Lord. It's the only thing I have to go on.
{Give 50 Rations.} I wish to give an offering to Baldr for good fortune.
Ketill withdraws his knife, and Asleifr falls forward, out of Nefja's embrace, and lands face first in the mud. Dead.
Step forward, I say! I always wanted to slay a giant! I hope he's fat and slow... more for my axe to bite into!
You'd better keep moving, heathen! Go on then!
Aye, this is the right thing to do. He's a good lad, he'll be a worthy successor.
Ketill places a hand on your shoulder.
Fine. You don't want my coins, I'll find my medicine elsewhere.
This is a nid-pole. It's a powerful curse.
Well if you need the pier that much, who am I to deny it. You've got yourselves a deal!
Hrodgærda can't quite hide the smirk in her voice.
{Check their pockets.}
He takes a couple of steps back, dies on his feet, and is immediately reborn with a thick layer of granite over his skin.
Wada pours himself a cup of wine and sinks unto a stool, a vague gesture towards the flask your only invitation to partake.
He doesn't look completely convinced.
The multilingual monk casts a hopeful glance at you as you turn your back on the village elder.
Sigmundr opens the tap of a cask and fills a large rowan-bark cup to the brim before handing it to you. He then fills one for himself as your companions gather around you.
I'll be all right!
I have decided to rule in favour of [Player:Name] [Player:Lastname] of Skjern.
I'm here to fight you, as agreed. Are you ready?
That trap's barely hidden.
I... miss it at times. There is serenity in such an ordered existence. But even if exaltation is found within the walls of a monastery, [i]knowledge[/i] is found on the road.
Stolen Sword
I'm an ealdorman under King Osred - a noble, ruling over a small shire to the south. But Osred is not my sovereign.
It's water under the bridge. Where do you want me?
So... how can I help the beautiful mistress? I take it from the way you carry yourself, you're not here to commission a brooch or a new pot for the kitchen?
Return to the old fisherman and tell him that his apprentice is dead.
Here's To The Future
It's a shame Osred was killed. He had a reputation for a wise but weak rule - a man who knew his subjects well and cared for them, but who had no stomach for war.
In the winter, the snow turns those mountains into clouds of shimmering light, and the fjords freeze almost to the bottom.

I won't hesitate to swear fealty to a woman who has earned her position as thegn, but when that position was granted to you simply because of the failures of the men who were meant to hold it? Then it is time for change.
It's a good thing you're on our side.
Speak nothing of it. You'll need it far more than I. If it saves your life one day, it'll be well worth the gifting.
Worry weighs heavily on his brow.
You said your name was [Player:Lastname]? I think your father's ship may have been by here. He had his brother with him, name of Grimulfr?
Sit down, and keep your mouth shut.
Meet Leofric in his camp at Hadrian's Wall.
Somehow it feels like it was always meant to happen. Here, at last, on a hot summer night in a strange land, that unspoken promise is fulfilled.
{Leave.}
{Present him with the corpse of Rikvi.}
Cillian is silent for a time, while he unpacks some jars from his sack. He hands you one and takes a few steps away to catch the nearest insect. With his back turned, it seems easier for him to talk.
A few years ago they decided they'd had it being subservient to anyone, so they organised under a lass called Aiblinn and declared independence.
He meets your eyes and holds your gaze.
Don't underestimate Aiblinn. She's a tough broad.
I was a fool. Naïve, to think you... any different from-- from your kinsmen.
Why'd she kick you out?
You shouldn't get your hopes up, Nefja. This is a long shot.
It seems he signed with me purely so he could skip town without anyone noticing his departure.
[Diver:Name] is gone for what seems like an eternity, with no sign of life. Eventually you realise [Diver:he/she] won't be coming back.
A young girl sits surrounded by pottery. She smiles warmly when you come near her stall.
I have no clue what that was, but let's grab what we came for and get out!
Oh my sweet girl! Your sister wants to leave us!
The young smith grins and wipes sweat from his forehead.
Hey... is there a problem?
Once again you save the day [Player:Name]!
The chronicles will show that his majesty was slain by the Viking [Player:Name] [Player:Lastname] of Skjern. Tragic.
When they grew up, they formed an army and conquered their original tribe, re-instating their father as king. Then they went off to found a new city.
Hliføy is still tending to her smithy, working on some repairs to a finely crafted sword.
Here it is - what a prize!
I've picked up a few things from Hulda.
Though a smile rests on the man's lips, there is no hint of it in his eyes.
Talorc doesn't look entirely happy about it, but he does set off towards the back of the village where Cillian is tied up.

The next morning, as you're packing up, you notice some valuables missing, most likely stolen by the missing thrall. As you start to move out, one of the other thralls finds a coin on the ground, which she's quick to return to you.

A pair of dour eyes regard you suspiciously from beneath bushy brows. The old man before you is lanky and slight, and though most of his lank hair is grey or white, streaks of ginger-red remain stubbornly visible.
I figured you wouldn't have followed me all the way here if you thought otherwise.
Do you have it? Did you bring the eagle?
The one you stole?
Would you now?
I'm going to lose mom too. I'm certain of it. I think it's the same [i]fucking[/i] curse that took Eyfura from us.
Some travellers had made camp in the forest near his house. It looks like they killed him before they moved on.
All sentimentality is gone from Caustantin's voice.
Better him than you, boy.
Disgusted, the woman spits on the earth between you.
Ancient Shield
I slept with you because I wanted to, Steinn. I'll be pleased to gain your allegiance, but you don't owe me anything.
Awesome, thanks.
It's a trap!
We wish to become legionnaires.
Come back when the people know you as a friend of the King.
We attempted to mediate between the nuns and a group of travellers from Mercia. Desperate, the Mercians attacked. We attempted to intervene, but to no avail.
Then you will be kept as my prisoner until I kill him.
May you find peace in the afterlife.
Stay away from that there barrow. Strange rites and odd noises.
My worry is that Skakki alone cannot foil [Player:him/her]. With your permission, I'll go as well.
You've lived here your whole life? Wouldn't you like to get out and see the world?
Talk to your father.
They'll quickly forget about us, they have bigger fish to fry.
Tears of shame glisten in Dubglas' eyes.
Then we shall call her Bygul. Velkomin to the hird, little one.
I've got a new family now. This amulet has protected me since I was born, and now it'll protect you when you leave.
This is, uhm, [Player:Name] of Skjern. [Player:He/She] has some questions?
Erlingr's wife Hjørdis walks up to you, back straight, and looks you straight in the eyes. You can tell she's been crying, but her voice is strong.
It takes more than that to kill an Ulfhedinn!
You locate Hrodgærda among the remains of her men. She's clutching a nasty wound, and she watches you silently with an intensity you've never seen in her before.
Go on through.
[Optimist:Name] puts a hand on your shoulder.
Do you let your dogs roam at night?
I've got the big one.
Oh, I'm... I'm sure that's not true, my child. You're stronger and wiser now than when you set out. That counts for something.
{Put the tablets together.}
Come on... pay up.
This place is so flat! Have you ever noticed? It's like the sky is ten times higher than it is back home.

Jarl Ragnhildr sent this sword after your father's funeral with her compliments for the way you handled Erlingr's sons. Runes delicately engraved along its narrow crossguard spell the name "Blood-Ice"
How do we know it's even still here? This stone was written ages ago.
[i]Horse shit[/i].
May the Lord not watch your actions too closely, Viking, and fare the well!
No one ever comes here willingly.
I had beaten Leofric before, it was no problem to do so again.
Not much for the likes of you in this neck of the woods.
Got anyone waiting for you at home?
Watch your step then, friends. Hopefully you'll find where you need to go soon.
With Grainne dead, Caustantin is the only commander left among with full authority over the Picts - the clans will follow no one else.
I wish they'd just leave!
I'm satisfied with the current selection.
Children complain. The best among us act!
Nefja's voice is soft and full of concern.
You're a slave - it doesn't matter what you want. You need to remember that.
Remember Eydis told us about the ancient grave on Funen, where they say a king and a queen were buried with all their wealth?

You count more than ten people in the group ahead. As you hide between the brambles, however, you notice that four of them are clapped in chains and under guard. Their shoulders are hunched in defeat and their eyes full of fear.
Why should anyone be spared? We're here to show the Christians the full scope of our wrath.
Aye, I suppose my best armour "will just have to do". Please forgive my incompetence [i]your majesty[/i].
Dwarves or elves? You're joking.
Thieves!
That we start moving, and see how far it takes us. Take odd jobs when we need to, not necessarily carpentry.
Let's send these bikkju-sonar back where they came from!
It was only a matter of time before the locals got bold enough for this. We haven't made a lot of friends around here!
The deposed king pours himself a cup of ale and takes a large swig.
HAH! I admire your resolve! Very well.
Thank you for your story Myrddin. I hope we'll meet again.
The skald spreads her arms and spins once around herself. Her cheer is almost too intense.
Through the dense brush, [Finder:Name] emerges with a young slave firmly gripped in one hand, the other hand pressing a knife against the young man's abdomen.
We're ready.
Really? Then you've earned my respect.
Resolve the feud.
Yes, just give me what we agreed.
My whole life has been one long string of defeats. This will be the last. I never lived like a real man, but I can die like one.
It's a relic of the great empire that once ruled in the south.
I believe you. The speed of your progress is impressive. The Jarl of course has been following these developments with great interest.
Did something... change between you two? I kind of feel like the way he looks at you... changed somehow. I don't know. Watch your back, I guess.
When she smiled, everything else seemed colourless by comparison. When she laughed, there was no other sound in the world.
We uh, we're just passing through.
I'm sorry I took so long. You didn't have to come look for me.
The Pictavian army must be cleared out of those caves, and a path must be opened through Hadrian's Wall.
I assure you they are just that: [i]lies[/i]. We are [i]Christians[/i], and like all God's servants, killing is abhorrent to us.
Long into the night, the mead still flows and laughter and shouts fill the air. Your hirdmen go about their tasks with a content smile and a sway in their step.
What are they?
Your uncle Sighialmr didn't much like spears, so he didn't bring his with him on your father's last expedition. Sighialmr never returned from that trip, so now his spear is yours.
No Escape
I heard you exiled Asleifr. I think he would have served you well as a huscarl, but I can't blame you for not wanting him around.
I'm sorry. I thought--
The old witch disappears briefly into her burrow. When she emerges again, she's holding two small corked jars.
Who let the heathens in here?
The master-of-arms regards you with a guarded look.
You cannot take this course of action! This will be seen as a declaration of war against Northumbria!
Jardarr's entire body seems to sag with dismay.
We aren' fighters like you... we just wanted to live free...
While she considers your words, she rubs her arms to bring warmth to her old skin.
I'm so sorry my [Player:boy/girl]. We're out of options.
Peace? Horse-shit. You're your father's [Player:son/daughter], and your actions prove it. You would have become a Viking no matter what.
You! How are you here?! What did you do to our children?!
That was sloppy, Nefja. Real sloppy.
The young woman glances at Halfdanr and then lowers her voice, blushing furiously.
Finally they pick their seats according to size and arm strength, and turn to you, waiting. You can no longer postpone it - you need to pick a Bannerman.
Careful if you turn her down. Got a fragile heart - easy to crush.
Anything that washes up on the beach is ours. Sell it off to the village, or anyone else who's buying.
Viper-fast, she cuts off his right ear with an artful flourish of her seax. He manages a scream and a drawn-out whimper.
[Player:Velkominn/Velkomin], gracious thegn. Are you looking to restock your supplies?
You understand, of course, that I cannot reward you for returning emptyhanded. Your failure in this endeavour will bring me great difficulties in the coming days.
Repent!
We're looking for a hermit.

Thanks to your quick intervention, none of the thralls were killed in the fighting. They watch you warily, unsure of what fate you have in store for them. A young man, with only the sorry beginnings of a beard on his chin, steps forward tentatively.
Found yourself a good woman in that one. Not really a surprise, think the whole village has been waiting for you two to figure it out.
All the time. I used to sit on the bridge with my feet dangling over the water and look out across the ocean, wonder what's on the other side.
No thanks, I must be off.
Steinn returns brightly.
Make it quick.
It is high time somebody does! Nobody else here has the spine, the courage to stand up to their thegn, so it falls to me. It is time to act!

You barely feel the coarse bark of the tree against your back as Asleifr lifts you up and squeezes you against it. Years of tension is set ablaze and the fire burns you both up and crackles through the night.
I'd help, but I care for my own first. Until I've helped them, I'm afraid you'll wait.

Once on the other side once more you see that everyone else also makes it out of the water intact. Knowing the route to take, the less experiences swimmers were able to make the dive without running out of air.
That'll put a strain on Æthelred's relationship with the nobles. Not good.
He drives the pitchfork into the mud and leans on it.
Got it!
You are out of your mind. We're done here.
Finally hearing you when you're almost breathing down his neck, he turns around, jumps back, presses himself flat against the wall, and mutters in shock.
Of course the Church is richer than the village, but to invoke the wrath of God--
Nefja and Røskva are squatting next to the smoldering remains of the campfire, their attention raptly fixed on something on the ground between them.
The hunter is sitting on the moss-covered trunk of a fallen tree, idly kneading his bowstring between two fingers. A wounded buck lies in front of him, evidently the source of the blood you spotted.
Very good. Will there be anything else today?
That was truly pathetic.
You're back. Are you ready to hunt those wolves?
A secret meeting with vikings, you say. I wonder what schemes the old dog was up to. We may never find out.
You spin around just in time to see [Victim:Name] topple into the ditch. The soil along the edge is shot through with thin roots that have stolen away the stability of the ground.
If there is really such wealth to be found there, we should go and claim it before someone else does.
So Be It
Very well. Ljotr and I will keep an eye on them, I'll let you know if anything changes.
Always a pleasure doing business with you, [Player:Name].
Yes, I suppose with the present troubles I have to accept any help I can.
Where did [i]you[/i] come from?!
What was that?! Looks like you just volunteered to clean the shit-hole tonight!
Shit... shit! Well, I can hardly blame you. At least, if he has any sense, he'll run far away.
I know. Don't worry about it.
Røskva covers her smile with a hand. A strong blush fills her cheeks as her gaze moves down your body. Biting her lip nervously, she glides up to you and moves in for a kiss.
The monk seems to notice your foreign clothing and your weapons, but he does a good job of hiding his worry.
No! What have you done?! This isn't right!
Then I am very glad to have prevented it, but I didn't know there was a threat against you. You owe me no particular gratitude.
Of course. I'm just an old man, Cillian has his whole life ahead of him. 'Sides, I've taught him the important things.
With that, she saunters back to her tent with a little more sway in her steps than usual.
Take care of yourself out there kid.
Guards! They've stolen from the grave!
Eydis is already tossing sacks of supplies onto the beach, making ready to establish a camp.

Your father's last journey was bound for the British Isles. Less than half of his crew returned.
Be careful to avoid attacks of opportunity during combat. Moving out of a hex adjacent to an enemy will give that enemy a free attack.
In combat, you can activate/deactivate your abilities by pressing the numerical keys on your keyboard.
During conversations, be mindful of your choices, as many options will change your reputation.
The morale of your hirdmen affects their physical and mental resistances, so try to keep everybody happy.
When your hirdmen become incapacitated during combat, the longer they stay down, the higher the risk of an injury.
Sustaining injuries does not put hirdmen out of action, but they will incur penalties in and out of combat.
If you lose track of your characters during gameplay, press F to center the camera on them.
A hirdman is anyone who travels with you and fights beside you. Your huscarls are those especially close and trusted warriors that serve you.
Equipment can be damaged during combat and will need to be repaired when you make camp.
Flanking bonus damage bypasses the target's Damage Reduction completely, making flanking attacks particularly powerful against well armoured enemies.
Each character can carry two sets of items and can freely switch between them until they attack. This is particularly important for archers.
Travel takes time, and time is a resource that will run out eventually. Plan your travels carefully.
Campsites persist between each visit. Take good care of your camp - you may need to use it again later.
Traders' stocks are replenished every week when a new shipment comes in.
Keep an eye out for cairns. Finding them gives you 1 SP each.
The threat of Christian expansion encroaches upon Denmark from the Frankish Realm to the south.
You can change the difficulty at any time if you need a bit less challenge - or a little more.
The pagan clans of Scandinavia have had little contact with the Christian kingdoms of the British Isles... until now.
The "leidangr" (levy) army can be conscripted every 4 years. Each "skipreida" (ship district) must send one ship with crew for the levy.
Know the strengths and weaknesses of your hirdmen. Someone with low Perception will make a poor archer. A healer with low Sense is useless.
A male religious leader in the North Germanic pagan faith was called a "godi". The equivalent female title is "gydja".
If you leave your left-hand item slot empty, you will gain a 3 percent-point bonus to your Critical Chance.
Viking longships were characterised by their shallow draft, which made them very fast and permitted river navigation and beach landings.
Christianity was brought to Britain by the Romans, but was destroyed in the Saxon invasions. The Gregorian Mission reintroduced Christianity around 600 AD.
Enemies block line-of-sight for ranged attacks. Your own characters do not block each others' attacks.
100 Valuables is equivalent to 10 ørtug of silver, or 5 anglo-saxon Pence.
Two-handed weapons offer reach, which lets you engage enemies without being trapped by their attack of opportunity.
In Old Norse, "viking" was the word for an expedition as well as someone who undertook one. So in a sense, this game is called Expeditions: Expedition.
A jarl is just beneath the king in power, and may be appointed to rule in his place. A thegn is a local chieftain, who often holds responsibility for a ship.
A shieldmaiden is a woman who has chosen to fight as a warrior. Despite the name, they don't necessarily carry shields.
Standard ranged attacks apply Harried which reduces the target's damage reduction for one round. Abilities do not harry enemies.
Any characters who still have their attack action (red ring) when the turn ends will be Steadied, protecting them from being Harried by archers.
During combat, you can select your followers by pressing F1 - F12
The thegns of Jutland meet King Sigurdr Hring at the Althing on the autumn equinox - September 19. You must achieve your goals before then.

In the mountains of the north, there exists a cult of warriors who call themselves the Ulfhednar. They are said to be Odinn's special warriors, who wear little except the pelt of a wolf into battle and become impervious to steel or fire. Gunnarr, the giant with the wholly ironic byname "the Peaceful", claims to be one of these berserkers.\n\nGunnarr led a group of raiders from the northern trade hub Kaupang to the isle of Orkney in the west, where he had the misfortune to meet Skule Skullcleaver. Skule convinced Gunnarr to mount a raid against your village. He may not be the most predictable huscarl in your service, but one thing is certain: it is far better to have Gunnarr on your side than against you.

You've known Nefja and her sister Eyfura since you were children. Their late father Holmunn was among your father's closest huscarls, and the sisters were often left solely in the care of their mother while he was travelling with his thegn.

The twins grew apart from an early age - where Eyfura was always her mother's beautiful and delicate girl, Nefja took more after her father and would spend her days exploring the woods, playing in the moor, or fighting with the boys. As soon as she was old enough to hold a wooden stick, she started training to be a warrior.

Over the years, the fire that burns brightly inside Nefja has turned her into a disciplined shieldmaiden, and what she lacks in raw strength is more than made up for in deftness and resolve.

Though her title is Princess of the Kingdom of Cait, Aife has few of a princess's manners and none of the typical conceits. Cait is a poor and harsh country, and Aife was raised to be as resilient and determined as any of her father's subjects. As soon as she was old enough, she was sent to train with the famous warrior Grainne, whose tutelage has turned her into a skillful trapper.\n\nGifted from an early age with equal parts curiosity and courage, Aife decided almost on a whim to join your hird. It's clear that she harbours some fascination with you and your culture. It's fortunate then that she is such a considerable asset on the field of battle.

Eydis came to your village with her husband Alvaldr when they were young and recently married, to take over his uncle's farm on the outskirts of your homestead and start a family. In your childhood, she was a warm and bubbly woman who loved to entertain the children of the clan with stories of ancient treasures or by reciting poems about the gods.\n\nA disease claimed Alvaldr almost a decade ago, leaving her alone to raise the two sons he gave her. Now her only concern is the safety and prosperity of her children. Since both of them are now old enough to tend to the farm, she has asked to join you on your expedition to the isles across the sea, that she might bring great wealth home and build a better future for her sons.

Asleifr is a distant cousin, the favourite son of another family in your clan. Leadership of the clan has passed back and forth between your family and his for generations, but although your father won the seat of thegn from Asleifr's father, Grimvardr served your father dutifully for years afterwards.\n\nFrom Grimvardr, Asleifr was instilled with an overwhelming sense of honour and duty. Asleifr has been raised as a strong and skilled warrior who wants nothing more from life than to serve and protect his family and his clan. To that purpose, he was compelled to challenge your claim to your father's throne, seeing you as weak and undeserving of leadership. In your duel, he was convinced otherwise, and he is now sworn to serve you on your travels to the isles across the sea.

Morcant is a brother of the Monkwearmouth monastery and spent his youth in diligent study and contemplation. He has immense respect for the learned and was inspired by his senior Bede to seek knowledge and codify it as an expression of faith and wonder of God's work.\n\nHe spent several years wandering the Northumbrian countryside, tending to and teaching the people. It was during these travels that he developed his fascination with pagan beliefs and sought to preserve them. In his eyes, these rites and stories inform the unenlightened grasping blindly for the illumination of God's truth - and through understanding them, he hopes to ease their transition into the true faith.

As a babe, Røskva was left in a basket in the bog outside your homestead - to this day, no one knows who her parents were, or why they decided to leave her to the carrion birds. To Røskva's great fortune, the old witch Hulda - herself childless - found the newborn girl and decided to raise Røskva as her apprentice.\n\nRøskva is still young, but she is already wise to the uses of plants and the whims of spirits. The young witch is a deft and compassionate healer, but she has no qualms with deadly poisons and cruel curses. After a score of winters first in the care of an old crone, then caring for the crone in turn, Røskva is keen to leave the village and seek new knowledge in distant lands.

Your father brought Ketill back home from one of his journeys in the north. The dark-haired boy had seen no more than eight winters at the time, and he had a shy and brooding demeanour about him then. Your father never adequately explained how he came to be responsible for the kid, but at the thegn's request, Ketill was taken in by the clan and raised as an orphan.\n\nKetill gradually came out of his shell, and being about the same age, you became fast friends. Ketill grew up to be a lean young man, whose soft step and keen eyes have made him a skillful hunter. Far from the quiet boy your father brought home with him, Ketill has come to wield a charming smile and a disarming wit. He is a good friend and a loyal huscarl who will follow you wherever you ask of him.

[size="16"]Block Chance[/size]\nDetermines how likely you are to block an attack with a shield, so the shield will take the damage instead of you.
[size="16"]Accuracy[/size]\nDetermines the maximum accuracy for ranged attacks. This drops by 6 points per hex of distance to the target, and the final hit chance can never exceed 95%.
[size="16"]Critical Chance[/size]\nDetermines the likelihood of landing a critical hit, which multiplies the damage by the critical modifier of the equipped weapon.
[size="16"]Damage[/size]\nDamage is your [color="lightblue"]Base Damage[/color], plus the damage of the currently equipped weapon.
[size="16"]Movement[/size]\nThe amount of hexes you can move during combat while still performing an attack. Armours can add penalties to this, making the unit able to move less hexes.

[size="16"]Damage Reduction (DR)[/size]\nDamage Reduction determines the amount of damage subtracted from incoming attacks. This might be different between melee and ranged attacks, depending on the equipped gear.
[size="16"]Stamina[/size]\nDetermines how many hours a character can go before becoming Fatigued. Getting two shifts of sleep at camp will reset the timer.

[size="16"]Hitpoints (HP)[/size]\nDetermines the amount of damage a character can sustain before getting [color="yellow"]Incapacitated[/color]. Hitpoints replenish after each fight, but characters will suffer injuries if incapacitated for too long.
[size="16"]Discipline[/size]\nDetermines the chance of resisting negative mental and physical effects.
[size="16"]Physical Resistance[/size]\nDetermines the chance of resisting negative physical effects. Derived from Strength and Morale. Shields can bolster this value.
[size="16"]Mental Resistance[/size]\nDetermines the chance of resisting negative mental effects. Derived from Sense and Morale. Helmets can bolster this value.
[size="16"]Morale[/size]\nDetermines the confidence of a character on a scale from -10 to 10. Affects physical and mental resistances.
Injuries can be treated during camping by assigning the task to a person who is versed in the art of healing.

[size="16"]Strength[/size]\nDetermines [color="lightblue"]Base Damage[/color] with axes and swords and affects [color="lightblue"]Physical Resistance[/color]. Strength is essential for warriors, and will occasionally enable knockouts and other physical feats in dialogue.

[size="16"]Endurance[/size]\nDetermines [color="lightblue"]Hitpoints[/color], [color="lightblue"]Base Damage Reduction[/color], [color="lightblue"]Block Chance[/color] with shields, and affects [color="lightblue"]Stamina[/color]. Endurance is of utmost importance to front-line fighters.

[size="16"]Finesse[/size]\nDetermines [color="lightblue"]Base Damage[/color] with knives and spears and [color="lightblue"]Critical Chance[/color] with all weapons. Finesse is important to ranged characters and fast-handed rogues, and can occasionally be used for surprise attacks in dialogue.
[size="16"]Perception[/size]\nDetermines [color="lightblue"]Accuracy[/color] with ranged weapons. Perception is crucial to archers, and will often reveal additional information during dialogue.

[size="16"]Sense[/size]\nAffects [color="lightblue"]Mental Resistance[/color] and [color="lightblue"]Stamina[/color]. Sense is fundamental to witches, skalds, and other support characters, and can often be used for persuasion in dialogue.

[size="16"]Morale[/size]\nAffects [color="lightblue"]Physical Resistance[/color] and [color="lightblue"]Mental Resistance[/color]. Morale represents the confidence of a character on a scale from -10 to 10.

Simple coats of layered cloth protect against glancing blows without restricting the wearer's movement, but it isn't much better than regular clothes.
Cured hide layered around the chest and back and padded with fur protects well against light cuts and impacts, but does restrict the wearer's movement slighty.
Laced rows of boiled leather platelets protect better than cloth and simple hide without restricting movement any more than hide armour.
A shirt of interlocking iron rings offers excellent protection against all weapons, but the coat is quite heavy and significantly restricts movement.
Fur Helmet
Leather Helmet
Steel Cap Helmet
Aventailed Helmet
Masked Helmet
These primitive fur helmets are easy to make, but not as robust as more advanced designs.
Cured leather helmets offer decent protection from glancing blows.
Steel cap helmets require great expertise to produce, but can take a lot of punishment.
Some armourers have found that attaching a curtain of ring mail to steel helmets is an easy way to offer extra protection.
Adding goggles and a nose guard to an aventailed helmet not only yields a little more protection, but looks very impressive.

Bearded Axe
Broad Axe
Battle Axe
Crucible Steel Axe
Simple utility axe intended for domestic work.
One step up from a tool axe, the bearded design makes it easier to use the axe in a fight.
A broader axe-head makes it easier to inflict damage on shields and flesh.
This design is the pinnacle of axes for combat use, facilitating all manner of tricks and unpleasantries.
Few smiths know how to forge steel in a crucible. Here the technique has yielded an axe of unparallelled durability.

A simple bow made from the wood of a willow tree. Useful for hunting animals, but not as good against humans.
Birch wood is strong and flexible, and yields an excellent hunting bow which is quite serviceable in combat.
A well built pine bow strung with horse-hair of matching quality, with a comfortable grip that ensures stability at full draw.
This fine bow is made from the wood of an elm tree. It is flexible and strong - a deadly weapon in the hands of a trained archer.
The wood of a yew is perfectly suited for a war-bow. This is a powerful and sturdy weapon, decorated with a fine grip and the highest quality bow string.

A broader axe-head makes it easier to inflict damage on shields and flesh.
This design is the pinnacle of axes for combat use, facilitating all manner of tricks and unpleasantries.

Narrow Seax
Light Broad Seax
Heavy Broad Seax
Long Seax
Short one-edged blade of varying sharpness, attached to a wooden handle. Never leave home without one.
Long single-edged blade, just short enough to qualify as a knife, but long enough to do some serious damage.
The broader blade of this knife gives it more weight when slashing, and its point is not to be trifled with either.
An even heavier, longer, and thicker version of the already quite heavy, long, and thick seax.
This knife is very nearly a sword. Its lightly curved blade is strong enough to pry open armour like a clamshell.
Simple Spear
Winged Spear
Pattern-welded Spear
Pattern-welded Winged Spear
Crucible Steel Spear
Little more than a sharpened stick, the common spear is cheap and easy to use.
The tip of this one is cleverly shaped to pry through armour and offers limited slashing capabilities for the dextrous wielder.
Though pattern-welding a speartip might seem like overkill, the extra flexibility allows for more powerful and accurate thrusts.
Combining a clever design with masterful smithing technique, this spear is incredibly deadly in the right hands.
The quality of this spear elevates it from a common weapon to something resembling a religious relic.
Single-Edged Sword
Broadsword
Pattern-welded Single-Edged Sword
Pattern-welded Broadsword
Crucible Steel Sword
Swords have little use other than for taking lives, but they are very good for that purpose.
By broadening the blade and sharpening both edges, a powerful and versatile weapon has been produced.
Pattern-welding a sword requires a high degree of mastery over the forge, but you can't argue with the results.
Despite the size of its blade, this sword is light and perfectly balanced. It's ornate hilt rests comfortably in any hand.
The state of the art of European smithing has produced a beautiful blade that feels like it could cut through a rock as easily as snow.
Hemp Sling
Flax Sling
Wool Sling
Gripped Flax Sling
Gripped Wool Sling
It may not be an elegant weapon, but a stone to the face at high speed will get the job done more often than not.
A stronger string and an improved release mechanism allows this sling to impart more power on each throw.
Wool spun tightly into a longer string, fitted with a better designed cradle for the projectile, makes this sling surprisingly powerful.
An unusual amount of ingenuity has gone into the creation of this sling. Its comfortable grip and carefully calibrated cradle makes it a joy to use.
This sling is so well made, so carefully designed, that comparing it to other weapons of its type is almost an insult.

Fir Shield
Padded Pine Shield
Padded Fir Shield
Padded Yew Shield
Pine isn't the best wood for a shield, but it's abundant and it certainly beats blocking a blow with your arm.
Made from a fir cut down in its prime, this shield is tougher than its pine counterparts without adding too much weight.
Padding a pine shield with cured leather improves the structural integrity of the shield significantly and protects against slinters.
This durable leather-padded fir shield has been further improved by reinforcing the areas where its grip connects to the wood.
Shields like this hang behind the thrones of kings. With its sturdy build and beautifully painted cured leather, it might stop a charging bull.
